papers.title: Nonstabilizerness as a diagnostic of criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate nonstabilizerness, also known as “magic”, to understand criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems. Our focus is on parity-time (PT)-symmetric spin chains, specifically the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising and XX models. We calculate stabilizer R…

papers.title: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
papers.abstract: Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource. Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states. For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.

papers.title: Entanglement Asymmetry and Asymmetry Contour under Boundary Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: We investigate how symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields affect magnetization and Rényi-2 entanglement asymmetry (EA) in the transverse-field Ising model. For the ground state, magnetization exhibits qualitatively distinct behaviors in the ordered and disordered phases. EA also exhibits phase-dependent behavior, which is well captured by the lower and upper bounds derived in this work. In the critical regime, both magnetization and EA exhibit behavior qualitatively consistent with the field-theoretical predictions for a related setup. We also study boundary-quench dynamics and find that magnetization propagates from the boundary into the bulk with a velocity consistent with the maximum quasiparticle velocity. In contrast, because EA is a subsystem-integrated quantity, its spatial structure is not directly resolved. We therefore introduce the asymmetry contour, a contour-like finite-difference quantity that provides a spatially resolved characterization of the symmetry-breaking information encoded in the reduced density matrix. The resulting contour is complementary to the local magnetization, retaining sensitivity to nonlocal many-body correlations while its dynamics also reflects the underlying quasiparticle propagation. These results show how EA and its contour can provide complementary information-theoretic characterizations of symmetry breaking and its spatial structure.

papers.title: Control of multipartite entanglement through anisotropy against thermal noise
papers.abstract: This Letter shows that the robustness of multipartite entanglement required for quantum computing platforms can be protected against thermal noise by tuning the interaction anisotropy in many-body systems. Focusing on both generalized Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger and generalized W states, this work reveals distinct survival regions of multipartite entanglement for suitable ranges of anisotropy.

papers.title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
papers.abstract: Pauli-based computation (PBC) is a measurement-based model of quantum computation that samples from output distributions of universal Clifford+$T$ circuits. Here, we provide a normal form (NF) that completely characterizes its adaptive and entanglement structures. These insights unify PBC with one-way quantum computing as dual or `time-reversed' counterparts. We use the NF to advance strategies for distributed computation and investigate magic-state injection rates. We also demonstrate an exponential improvement in the detection of unnecessary magic-state qubits, allowing their efficient removal. Our NF further enables ahead-of-time circuit compilation using PBC, reducing CNOT gate count and quantum memory of random quantum circuits on average by 50% and 40%, respectively, beating other state-of-the-art compilers.

papers.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
papers.abstract: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.

papers.title: Range-controlled entanglement in Lindbladian skin states of monitored fermions
papers.abstract: Reservoir engineering can stabilize states inaccessible to unitary dynamics. Directed particle-conserving dissipation creates Lindbladian skin states, where Pauli exclusion turns edge accumulation into a many-body density imbalance. In a monitored fermion chain with tunable hopping range, we identif…

papers.title: Tripartite entanglement in ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}→t\overline{t}Z$
papers.abstract: Multipartite entanglement is a uniquely quantum form of correlation that captures collective properties of a composite quantum state beyond those encoded in its bipartite subsystems. We investigate this phenomenon in the process e+e−→tt¯Z at a future lepton collider, where the final-state spins span…

papers.title: Noise-tolerant macroscopic magnon-phonon quantum entanglement and nonreciprocity via Duffing nonlinearity and the Barnett effect
papers.abstract: We study macroscopic magnon–phonon quantum entanglement in a magnomechanical system with Duffing nonlinearity and nonreciprocity induced by Barnett effect. When two degenerate phonon modes are coupled to a magnon mode supported by the yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere, the darkmode effect suppresses …

papers.title: Entanglement percolation enhanced by the power of choice
papers.abstract: Quantum communication networks are best supported by maximally entangled states, but imperfections in entanglement generation and distribution generally limit the distributed states to being only partially entangled. Therefore, protocols typically consisting of local operations and classical communi…

papers.title: Two-Layer Verification for Fault-Tolerant Magic-State Preparation in High-Rate Quantum Codes
papers.abstract: Encoded magic states are essential for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their resource-efficient preparation in high-rate quantum codes remains challenging. To address this limitation, we propose two-layer verification, which combines local verification of independently prepared subblocks with logical verification after their embedding into a target code. This hierarchy detects harmful error patterns, including even-parity logical-eigenvalue flips that are invisible to a collective product check alone. We demonstrate this scheme for a $[[21,3,5]]$ code by constructing a circuit that embeds three verified seven-qubit Steane-code magic states into the target code. Circuit-level simulations of $T$- and $S$-state preparation show logical-error suppression consistent with the code distance. These results demonstrate the potential of two-layer verification as a design principle for reliable magic-state preparation in quantum codes encoding multiple logical qubits.

papers.title: Real-space construction and selection rules of center-of-mass momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional many-body lattices
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for the real-space construction of center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional (2D) quantum many-body systems. Unlike standard momentum-space approaches, our real-space formalism explicitly captures the non-uniformity of cyclic subspace dimensions, which are fundamentally governed by the spatial symmetries of the many-body configurations and particle statistics. We demonstrate that performing 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states naturally induces non-trivial translation phase factors associated with the characters of these stabilizer subgroups, leading to a renormalization of permissible momentum values. Notably, we identify an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling in highly symmetric particle distributions, where the permissible momentum values in one direction are strictly constrained by those in the perpendicular direction. We emphasize the algorithmic necessity of this coupling, as neglecting it leads to missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations. Concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the practical implementation and physical consequences of this framework.

papers.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.

papers.title: Noise-Assisted Quantum Entanglement: Memory-Enhanced Coherence in Stochastic Jaynes-Cummings Dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate qubit entanglement dynamics in a two-qubit cavity system with stochastically fluctuating coupling strength, comparing white noise (Markovian) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise (non-Markovian) processes. We analytically solve the system dynamics for both Fock and coherent cavity states and systematically characterize how initial qubit configurations affect entanglement generation and preservation. Our results reveal distinct dynamical regimes: in the Fock-state cavity, initial states in the single-excitation subspace generate robust qubit entanglement in decoherence-free subspaces, while initially entangled states in the double-excitation subspace exhibit inevitable decay without protective symmetries. For coherent cavities, we identify a critical photon-number threshold in the intermediate coherent-state amplitude regime where dynamics transition from low-frequency to high-frequency entanglement oscillations, while universal entanglement loss occurs at large amplitudes. Remarkable resilience against entanglement sudden death emerges under strong non-Markovian noise with long correlation times, where repeated revivals occur. These findings establish cavity photon statistics and environmental memory time as key control parameters for engineering qubit entanglement dynamics in qubit-cavity systems, revealing how system-environment correlations govern quantum information preservation.

papers.title: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
papers.abstract: How much entanglement can two distant laboratories share when their connection is noisy? We relate this question to deciding which of two quantum hypotheses is present. Our one-shot bounds apply to entanglement generation over a quantum channel and to one-way entanglement distillation from a shared state. We use Cheng's trace inequality to bound the infidelity of a Petz decoder in terms of a binary hypothesis testing cost. Applying the inequality before averaging over codes reduces the error analysis to computing a second moment of random subspaces. The proof covers every integer target dimension and treats rank-deficient states explicitly. A corollary expresses the achievable entanglement through hypothesis-testing coherent information, with a single logarithmic error slack and exact integer rounding. We also prove an error-preserving conversion from entanglement generation codes to entanglement transmission codes: the target dimension decreases by only a constant factor at fixed error, and the decoder is the original decoder followed by local processing. Consequently, for both entanglement generation and entanglement transmission, arbitrary pure reference-input states yield the same coherent-information rate, second-order Gaussian correction at the original error tolerance, and explicit achievable logarithmic remainder. For commuting testing hypotheses, the logarithmic remainder improves to a constant. These results give a direct route from binary distinguishability to explicit recovery guarantees and finite-resource quantum communication rates.

papers.title: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
papers.abstract: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.

papers.title: Can Entanglement-Induced Feature-Map Designs Improve Projected Quantum Kernels?
papers.abstract: Projected quantum kernels (PQKs) have emerged as a notable approach to circumvent the hardness of machine learning tasks arising from the exponential dimensionality of the quantum Hilbert space. However, recent PQK studies often rely heavily on extensive classical hyperparameter tuning of the radial basis function (RBF) kernel parameter and the support vector machine regularization parameter. The extensive tuning can mask the true representational power of the underlying PQKs induced by quantum feature maps, which has not been explored in detail. Thus, this work aims to expose the structural capabilities of PQKs by isolating and evaluating their native inductive bias through comparisons between untuned and tuned PQKs against the RBF baseline. Furthermore, we propose novel quantum feature maps that leverage two-qubit entanglement to capture multivariate correlations in IoT data. The results show that extensive tuning can lead to competitive performance architectures, while our proposed entanglement topologies exhibit a significantly stronger native inductive bias. This reveals that superior quantum architectural design can yield structurally better PQKs with improvements arising from quantum-mechanical properties rather than from classical hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
papers.abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

papers.title: The limits of magic-state distillation
papers.abstract: Magic-state factories are a major cost of fault-tolerant quantum computing, yet how few noisy inputs they need is known only for restricted protocols. We show that, for tolerating input faults, any stabilizer protocol, however adaptive, postselected or multistage, is no better than a projection onto one stabilizer code, and that for rational targets a fault pattern is harmful exactly when its complement is. Searches over all codes show that quadratic distillation of one T state needs exactly nine inputs and that the eight-input CCZ factory is optimal. At order $d$, one T state needs $n\geq2d$.

papers.title: Detecting multilevel entanglement from light-based entanglement witnesses
papers.abstract: We introduce a set of electric-field-based inequalities capable of detecting multilevel entanglement from a system of N quantum emitters. We determine that the polarization channel as well as the direction of detection can enhance entanglement detection, a feature specific to multilevel systems. We …

papers.title: Hierarchical Reduction of Invariant Subspaces: From Fragmentation to Many-Body Scars
papers.abstract: We investigate a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures connecting Hilbert-space fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. For spin chains with fragmented spin-$1/2$ subspaces and their local deformations, we show, using the spin-$1$ $XXC$ chain as a representative example, how successive local deformations reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an implicitly embedded spin-$1/2$ invariant space and ultimately to a single scar tower, connecting the $XXC$, perturbed $XXC$, and spin-$1$ $XY$ scar models. Through the intermediate embedded space, local dynamics couples states from distinct frozen irreducible-string sectors and selects a new decomposition into representations, from which smaller invariant spaces can be retained. We also establish a rigidity constraint on isolating nonsymmetric towers and a constructive correspondence that transfers a reduction between locally realizable representations of the embedded dynamics. The latter demonstrates that the reduction hierarchy can be transferred through a unitary transformation within the embedded subspace, yielding an exact scar tower built on a Néel reference state without requiring unitary equivalence of the full Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
papers.abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by ${}_S\langle Ψ| \hatψ(x)\hatψ(x') | Ψ\rangle_S$, where $|Ψ\rangle_S$ is the superconducting state, and where $\hatψ(x)$ is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al.\ regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J.\ Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

papers.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
papers.abstract: Majorana drew a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the Bloch sphere, antipodal to the zeros of its overlap with spin coherent states. Projecting only one qubit of a general state leaves the others in a state that varies with direction. Its entanglement invariants are eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix and form bands over the sphere. Exceptional points appear, without gain or loss, where the entanglement family of the rest changes. Circling one exchanges two bands, so the bands form one Riemann surface. At five qubits it fixes the entanglement class up to finitely many choices.

papers.title: Experimental Tomography of Quantum Many-Body Hamiltonians in Solids via Thermalization
papers.abstract: Characterizing the unknown Hamiltonian of a quantum many-body system is essential for exploring fundamental physical phenomena and advancing frontier quantum technologies. However, the complexity of many-body interactions and limited control capabilities in realistic experimental systems render this…

papers.title: Microscopically informed self-consistent multi-resolvent closure for dense many-body spectra
papers.abstract: The exact multi-resolvent hierarchy of dense many-body spectra encodes higher-order spectral-weight correlations, but closing it predictively for interacting Hamiltonians remains a challenge. We introduce the multi-resolvent self-consistency (MRSC) equations, which separate an exact algebraic hierarchy from an approximate finite-parameter closure. The exact Feshbach geometric identity organizes r-resolvent cumulants into a ladder over irreducible vertices Gamma^(r), and the projected hierarchy expresses those vertices as functionals of the cumulants. The closure works in finite parameters: a connectivity basis organizes a general Hamiltonian's seed into class amplitudes, and a causal r-fold Stieltjes representation with a moment-field identity reduce moment matching to a finite-dimensional problem closed at a predictive fixed point. On the free-fermion benchmark the tested exact identities are reproduced and the Faddeeva closure is recovered at r=1. In a blind test on the interacting Ising chain, with the exact two-resolvent data withheld, the Hamiltonian-derived closure predicts the tested probes to 0.35%-0.97%. At the observable level the exact two-resolvent sector supplies a sign-correct, energy-resolved correction to the single-resolvent baseline for the off-diagonal eigenstate-thermalization-hypothesis (ETH) variance, of order one relative to it. Closure errors organize hierarchically: a level-by-level deficit decomposition, anchor measurements of the isolatable terms, and an explicit propagation bound. The same moments further yield a diagnostic chain for the window conditions of local rotational invariance -- an exact drift-kernel identity, a proven single-state identifiability boundary, and a transferability census over couplings and realizations -- a finite-order framework, not a proof of universal emergence.

papers.title: Entanglement dynamics by nonunitary local operator quenches in a 2D holographic CFT
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the time evolution of entanglement entropy and mutual information for the spatially-infinite systems where we act with a primary operator on the vacuum state and then time-evolve it with the sequence of the Euclidean and Lorentzian time evolutions. Two-dimensional holog…

papers.abstract: We address momentum entanglement in Higgs decays to weak boson pairs, H → WW, ZZ, by discretising momentum space. papers.title: Quantum randomness certification with untrusted measurements and few probe states
papers.abstract: We present a scheme for semi-device-independent quantum randomness certification from an untrusted measurement device and a trusted source and demonstrate it experimentally. No assumptions about noise or imperfections in the measurement are required and the scheme is simple to implement with existin…

papers.title: Can mirror symmetry challenge local realism? Probing photon entanglement from positronium via Compton scattering
papers.abstract: This study investigates photon entanglement generated from parapositronium decay by analyzing azimuthal correlations after the double Compton scattering with stationary electrons. We introduce a normalized correlation observable O1=cos(2ϕ1−2ϕ2)/C1 to witness entanglement. In the absence of decoheren…

papers.title: Syndrome resampling enhances quantum error correction thresholds
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) enables fault-tolerant quantum computation but requires operating quantum hardware at physical error rates below code-dependent thresholds, which remains challenging for current devices. We introduce syndrome resampling, a general method that increases QEC thresholds o…

papers.title: Radiative spin caloritronics in nonreciprocal many-body systems
papers.abstract: We predict the spin thermal Hall effect in nonreciprocal magneto-optical many-body systems, in which a longitudinal radiative heat current generates a transverse accumulation of the spin angular momentum carried by thermal photons. We show that this effect and the inverse spin thermal Hall effect co…

papers.title: Stabilizer Rényi moments beyond entanglement
papers.abstract: Stabilizer Rényi moments depend on a choice of operator basis and need not be determined by entanglement spectra. In this paper, we study their spatial decay in critical quantum chains described by two-dimensional conformal field theories. We derive an exact entanglement baseline for reductions of pure stabilizer states and a symmetry selection rule for the charged contribution at fixed support. An exact Ising example shows that an on-site rotation changes the full decay exponent while preserving every subsystem entanglement spectrum. For growing Ising intervals at index two, we obtain an exact Pfaffian representation and compare the charged amplitude with a candidate conformal boundary calculation. The data support this prediction, but its identification with the lattice limit still requires endpoint matching and control of the order of limits.

papers.title: Microscopic Bipartition and Macroscopic Symmetry in a Rényi Entanglement Ensemble
papers.abstract: Universal information extracted from entanglement at a critical point is commonly associated with the long-distance properties of the bulk state, while microscopic details of a lattice bipartition are expected to be washed out under coarse graining. Counterintuitively, we show directly that such microscopic information can survive in the statistical ensemble that determines the second Rényi entropy and obviously change the physics there. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the square-lattice $J$-$Q_3$ model at the Néel--valence-bond-solid (VBS) transition, we measure magnetic and dimer order parameters in the Rényi-2 ensemble. For a standard axis-aligned bipartition, the VBS component perpendicular to the entanglement boundary remains finite in the thermodynamic extrapolation and is inequivalent to the parallel component, while the Néel order vanishes. For a $45^\circ$ tilted bipartition, in contrast, the two VBS components remain equivalent within numerical accuracy. We interpret this contrast in terms of the Rényi twist defect: the two bipartitions have the same bulk theory but realize different microscopic defect symmetries. Our results demonstrate that lattice information invisible to the bulk continuum theory alone can remain active in the long-distance Rényi ensemble, providing a microscopic explanation for the strong bipartition dependence previously observed in entanglement studies of deconfined criticality.

papers.title: Low-nonlinearity advantage of hollow-core fiber for wavelength multiplexing of quantum entanglement and classical DWDM signals
papers.abstract: Coexistence of classical and quantum light in optical fiber is a key requirement for scalable quantum networks. However, it is fundamentally limited by nonlinear crosstalk from intense classical signals. Hollow-core fiber (HCF), with its intrinsically low optical nonlinearity, offers a promising solution. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the coexistence of polarization-entangled photons with dense wavelength-division multiplexed (DWDM) classical signals with a total launch power of 11.2 dBm, and perform a direct comparison between equal-length single-mode fiber (SMF) and photonic-bandgap-based HCF deployed in a campus network. We observe that HCF suppresses background noise by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to SMF, while preserving high-fidelity entanglement distribution. Our results provide clear experimental evidence of the advantage of HCF and establish its potential as a transmission medium.

papers.title: A General Master Equation for Two Accelerated Detectors: Stationary States and Entanglement
papers.abstract: We derive a general Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan master equation for two co-located, uniformly accelerated two-level detectors weakly coupled to scalar fields in the Minkowski vacuum, retaining coherent and dissipative contributions for arbitrary orientations, field masses, and spacetime dimensions. For equal orientations, we determine stationary states and their entanglement for two couplings to massless fields in four dimensions: symmetric coupling yields acceleration-dependent concurrence, whereas rotating-wave coupling gives acceleration-independent concurrence.

papers.abstract: We study a random theory of semiclassical guiding center motion a many electron system in a strong magnetic field. papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the dynamical phase transition of the quantum O(N) model at large N leaves universal fingerprints in the infrared structure of the entanglement spectrum. While the leading contribution to the entanglement entropy at long time follows the conventional volume law associated with ba…

papers.abstract: Gravity-induced entanglement (GIE) experiments have been proposed as a theory-independent test of the quantum nature of gravity, on the strength of several no-go theorems concluding that GIE detection implies the gravitational interaction is either nonlocal or nonclassical. This is in apparent tensi…

papers.title: Freezing and shielding under global quenches for long-range interacting many-body systems
papers.abstract: This article reveals that previous observations, in which the nonequilibrium dynamics of long-range models mirror short-range systems under local quenches, reflect a universal feature of long-range interacting quantum systems. This is demonstrated by showing that this feature is also present under global quenches.

papers.title: Activating entanglement and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering from continuous-variable resources using witness-based measures
papers.abstract: Quantum resource theories identify resourceful states by their separation from a set of free states, but a general state-level operational meaning for this separation is often missing. We introduce bounded witness-based monotones for resource theories with closed free sets and show that they quantif…

papers.title: Erratum: Certification of genuine multipartite entanglement in spin ensembles with measurements of total angular momentum [Phys. Rev. A 109, 042402 (2024)]
Asymptotic scars arising from the remnants of quantum phase transitions
papers.abstract: Many-body localisation, Hilbert space fragmentation and quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are well-established mechanisms of ergodicity breaking in quantum systems. Recently, asymptotic quantum many-body scars (AQMBS), non-thermal states whose stability grows with system size, have been proposed theoretically and probed experimentally. Here, we show that AQMBS arise naturally as remnants of certain quantum phase transitions. For a broad class of frustration-free Hamiltonians, we prove that their gapless excitations survive deformation into a scarred Hamiltonian as states whose energy variance is bounded by the excitation gap. Consequently, the gapless excitations at a quantum critical point become AQMBS of the scarred Hamiltonian. Their fidelity relaxation time is then set by the critical scaling of the gap, determined by the dynamic critical exponent. Modelling the critical Fredkin and Motzkin chains and the two-dimensional PVBS model, we obtain AQMBS whose variances directly reflect the dynamic exponents of the underlying transitions. Where the gap of the Motzkin chain closes super-exponentially, we find exponentially stable AQMBS, for which we also observe numerical evidence of volume-law entanglement.

papers.title: QuantumMatterExplorer: An Autonomous Agent for the Discovery of Quantum Many-Body Phases of Matter
papers.abstract: Mapping the phase diagram of a new quantum Hamiltonian demands expert judgement at every step: which observables to measure, where in parameter space to compute, or how to separate genuine order from finite-size artefacts. We introduce QuantumMatterExplorer, an autonomous agent that takes only a Hamiltonian and its parameter ranges as input and returns a phase diagram obtained from its own numerical simulations. The agent is built on a large language model and is designed to reason over a long horizon, maintain a persistent written plan, and drive a set of computational tools, with density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations cross-checked against independent exact diagonalization. The agent combines a large language model with persistent planning, a library of expert computational-physics skills, and density-matrix renormalization group calculations validated against independent exact diagonalization. It adaptively selects quantities to evaluate, refines parameter scans, and performs finite-size analyses as evidence accumulates. After validating the approach on Hamiltonians with known transitions, we challenge it with a frustrated bilinear-biquadratic spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy, whose two-dimensional phase diagram was published only recently and is unlikely to appear in any training corpus. Given no hint about the expected physics, the agent proposes which observables to probe, and identifies candidate Néel, Haldane and dimerized phases, in broad agreement with the reference phase diagram. It also detects incommensurate correlations and infers the frustration-dependent geometry of the phase boundaries, all within an eight-hour compute budget. These results open a practical route to the autonomous computational discovery of new phases of quantum matter.

papers.title: Quantum Complexity and Stabilizer-State Expansions: From Pairing to Deformation in Fermionic Systems
papers.abstract: Understanding how collective phenomena such as pairing and deformation emerge in interacting fermionic systems, and how the correlations underlying them shape the resources required for their simulation, is a central challenge in many-body physics. We investigate various aspects of quantum complexity in a fermionic system exhibiting two main forms of collectivity, specifically deformation and pairing, through entanglement, non-stabilizerness, and fermionic non-Gaussianity. In the deformed phase, high entanglement coexists with low non-stabilizerness, while the superfluid pairing phase, by contrast, exhibits substantial multipartite entanglement and non-stabilizerness, together with maximal fermionic anti-flatness. In a second step we examine how to describe the phase diagram of the system in a classically scalable and symmetry-preserving way, by combining stabilizer-state expansion and variational basis optimization. A physics-guided decomposition of the Hamiltonian identifies the relevant stabilizer states, which can be constructed from graph states. A single stabilizer state captures the deformed phase to a large extent, and, although the number of stabilizer states required to describe the pairing phase grows exponentially with system size, a symmetry-preserving basis rotation yields a high-fidelity approximation using far fewer states. This rotated state can then serve as a practical starting point for quantum refinement.

papers.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
papers.abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase \(γ_n\). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is \(γ_n\)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.

papers.title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum architecture that achieves addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant logical in high-rate codes. The codes are obtained from the flexible concatenation of small-distance high-rate self-dual CSS codes. Addressable and parallel universal logic on the resulting $K$ logical qubits is injected by fault-tolerantly preparing and then consuming diverse logical $K$-qubit CSS stabilizer states and logical $\lvert H \rangle^{\otimes K}$ global magic states. Flag-at-origin is used to prepare the stabilizer resource states while a concatenated cultivation protocol prepares the global magic states. These resource states are consumed by Steane-QEC or Knill-QEC teleportation gadgets, which simultaneously perform quantum error correction. Any quantum algorithm with $T$-depth $D_T$ can be executed by consuming $12D_T$ or fewer resource states. We benchmark the fault-tolerant preparation of the resource states for several two-level concatenations of the $[[k+4,k,2]]$ H codes and the Hamming $[[15,7,3]]$ code. In particular, we find that the concatenated cultivation offers at least one order of magnitude spacetime reduction compared to cultivation in the surface code.

papers.title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
papers.abstract: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.

papers.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
papers.abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell-pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$. Remarkably, this optimal protocol can provide substantial memory reductions over existing heuristic approaches. In particular, for the path graph $P_n$ over $n$ users, Piecemaker protocol requires at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ qubits of peak persistent memory for \textit{every Bell-links generation order}, whereas under the order $(1,2,\ldots,n)$, our protocol requires only one persistent switch qubit. Finally, the same stabilizer-transition framework also provides a direct forward construction for sequential graph-state generation using the minimum number of quantum emitters, equal to the maximum of the height function.

papers.title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
papers.abstract: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.

papers.title: Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(π(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $π(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(π(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(π(P)+ε)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(π(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $π_d=π(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)λ_d\leπ_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $λ_d$ is the vertex Turán density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-π_d=\exp(-Θ(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\leπ_2\le2.15121$.

papers.title: CO$Φ$ - COmpiling PHotonics into dIgital quantum circuits
papers.abstract: Photonic and qubit-based (digital) approaches to quantum computing are largely regarded as separate paradigms. This article aims to bridge these paradigms by developing a method for mapping quantum-optical systems onto qubit-based quantum circuits. The key ingredient enabling this mapping is the introduction of a truncation of the Fock space describing single-mode optical states. Within this framework, representations of basic photonic operations are developed, including the phase-rotation operator, the displacement operator, the squeezing operator, and the beam splitter. Explicit quantum circuit constructions are provided for Fock-space truncations of dimension $N=2$ and $N=4$. We discuss benchmarking of the implemented operations and identify the regime of applicability and the limitations of the proposed method. The presented results can be used to simulate quantum optical circuits on qubit-based quantum computers, with special relevance to Gaussian Boson Sampling in the low-photon-number regime. To demonstrate the practical applicability of this approach, we complement the theoretical framework with a Python-based quantum programming tool CO$Φ$ that compiles Blackbird quantum-optics programs into qubit-based OpenQASM circuits using a truncated Fock-space encoding. The compiler is available on GitHub at https://github.com/Quantum-Cosmos-Lab/cophi.

papers.title: Bose Polarons as Relativistic Unruh-DeWitt Detectors: Entanglement Harvesting from Bose-Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: An impurity in a Bose-Einstein condensate with time-tunable coupling realizes an Unruh-DeWitt detector of the condensate’s effective relativistic phonon field.

papers.title: Fermion Scattering on Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: Resonant scattering links particle interactions to the formation and decay of unstable excitations. We develop a hybrid quantum-computing framework to study these dynamics through fermion--antifermion collisions. Our formulation of $(1+1)$-dimensional Yukawa theory encodes fermions in qubits and the scalar field in qumodes. We identify the operations needed for a photonic implementation and benchmark the dynamics with tensor-network simulations. Near resonance, we resolve the build-up of a localised scalar excitation and the subsequent partial return of energy to the fermions. Enhanced entanglement accompanies this exchange. Time-dependent correlator measurements reproduce the analytically predicted decay rate to a few percent precision, with energy scans exhibiting a resonance peak consistent with packet-averaged Breit--Wigner behaviour. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

papers.title: Exploiting the Weyl-Chamber Structure for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Compression
papers.abstract: Quantum circuit compression based on tensor networks enables long-time simulation of quantum many-body dynamics on near-term hardware. While Riemannian optimization has been successfully employed for this purpose, it typically optimizes over the manifold of generic two-qubit unitaries. Consequently, the resulting gates must still be synthesized into the hardware's native gate set via KAK decomposition, an overhead that partially negates the original compression gain. We show that Riemannian-optimized gates already exhibit a predictable Weyl structure: near-$R_{ZZ}$ for the Ising model and near-fSim for the Heisenberg XXZ model. Building on this insight, we investigate whether parameterized optimization directly over the native gate set can offer a beneficial trade-off between expressivity and circuit efficiency by reducing the circuit's dimensionality. When comparing the two approaches, we find that the small residual Weyl parameters neglected by the latter are essential for high compression of the Ising propagator, whereas for the Heisenberg propagator, the native XXZ structure can be exploited directly to build a more efficient compressed circuit.

papers.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
papers.abstract: Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone. This review introduces radiologists to five core quantum concepts, qubits, superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, and quantum circuits, and to the superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware platforms that define the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. We then summarize the quantum machine learning architectures most often applied to medical imaging (quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, variational quantum circuits, and quantum convolutional neural networks) and quantum image representations such as the flexible representation of quantum images (FRQI) and the novel enhanced quantum representation (NEQR). Reported applications include brain tumor classification and segmentation on MRI, pneumonia detection on chest radiographs, skin and breast lesion classification, CT and PET reconstruction, and ultrasound denoising. Nearly all published systems are hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators, and clinical deployment is not yet feasible. We conclude with current limitations and translational priorities for radiology.

papers.abstract: Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.

papers.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: We demonstrate high-fidelity logical qubit operations using \texttt{ibm\_phoenix}, a square-lattice array of 120 coupled superconducting qubits that are capable of fast reset. Using strategies to exclude underperforming components together with noise informed decoding, we routinely produce surface codes at distance-3 and distance-5 with logical error per round below 1\%. We demonstrate entanglement between two logical qubits, where logical Bell-state fidelities above 93\% are observed for entanglement created via lattice surgery. With three logical qubits and lattice surgery, we perform logical teleportation of a range of states and gates, observing fidelities in the range 78\% - 93\%. Using reset to reduce qubit leakage, we show that repeated rounds of stabilizer measurements continue to exhibit improvements in a stability experiment up to $\sim 2\cdot 10^{-7}$ over 170 measurement rounds.

papers.title: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
papers.abstract: A longstanding question in Bell nonlocality is whether finite-alphabet nonsignalling resources can reproduce the continuum of measurement correlations of partially entangled qubits. Here we resolve this problem by showing that every fixed pure two-qubit state admits an exact simulation of all local projective-measurement statistics using shared randomness and finitely many Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes, without communication or postselection. The boxes operate in parallel, with a worst-case bound independent of the measurement settings: at most $128\cot^4θ$ calls for the Schmidt state $\cosθ|00\rangle+\sinθ|11\rangle$, $0<θ<π/4$. The key is an exact finite-selection method that reduces input-dependent continuous sampling to a choice from a fixed-length shared random list, implemented through a finite PR-box network. The construction extends to arbitrary mixed two-qubit states and local binary-outcome POVMs. This reveals a fundamental separation between the continuity of quantum measurement correlations and the alphabet size of the resources needed to simulate them, shedding light on the resource-theoretic structure of Bell nonlocality.

papers.title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
papers.abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.

papers.title: Graphical Rigidity of Continuous Variable Graph States under Gaussian Local Transformations
papers.abstract: Multimode entangled pure Gaussian states are an essential resource for continuous variable (CV) quantum information processing. Menicucci et al. [2011] have shown how to describe them as graphs with complex adjacency matrices. Among such complex graph states (CGSs), quantum optics experimental setups straightforwardly display correlations described by purely imaginary graph states (iRGSs) whereas theoretical literature favors off-diagonal real graph state (RGS) descriptions, which actually reflect the entanglement structure in the infinite squeezing limit [Gonzalez-Arciniegas et al. 2021]. We study them beyond this ideal case, thus establishing in the finite squeezing regime an equivalence criterion for the generic case of CGSs through a graph propagating set of conditions which either finds a Gaussian Local Unitary (GLU) converting one state to another or gives a proof of impossibility if such a GLU does not exist. In the experimentally relevant case of the conversion between iRGSs and RGSs, the set of conditions results in simple relations between the topologies of the equivalent real and imaginary graphs. Finally, we show that the canonical forms of iRGSs and RGSs imply that the topology of the CV real and imaginary graph states are too rigid to admit any exact qumode local-addition analogue to the qubit complementation or qudit local-addition, thus demonstrating the non-existence of any exact qumode local-addition for these states. We however define an approximate one when the squeezing is strong enough.

papers.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
papers.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

papers.title: Mutual Information Across Quantum Reference Frame Perspectives
papers.abstract: In quantum information theory, standard notions typically presuppose a fixed partition of the world into subsystems, encoded in a tensor product structure of the Hilbert space. Yet, in some scenarios, the subsystem structure is not uniquely fixed. A case in point is the description of subsystems relative to different quantum reference frames (QRFs), where the tensor product structure, although fixed in a specific QRF, changes across different QRFs. Such a relativity of subsystems underlies many interesting features of QRFs, such as the relativity of entanglement, entropy, and coherence. It also raises a broader question: how do we compare the information across different subsystem perspectives, especially when the corresponding subsystem algebras overlap? Here, we propose a notion of quantum mutual information across different QRF perspectives, which captures the correlations between subsystems relative to different frames of reference. To do so, we focus on an algebraic definition of subsystems. Studying in detail the union and overlap between subsystem algebras relative to different QRFs, we find that the usual definition of mutual information in terms of the chain law overcounts the information associated to the overlap. Based on this insight, we propose a modified chain law and show that the resulting notion of mutual information satisfies subadditivity and connects naturally to other measures found in the literature [1]. Our investigations not only provide a way to quantify the relation between different QRF perspectives from an information-theoretic point of view but also sheds light on some important features of quantum information in absence of a fixed tensor product structure.

papers.abstract: Understanding quantum phases and phase transitions in the presence of symmetries is a central objective of quantum many-body physics. papers.abstract: Generalized Langevin equations (GLEs) provide a powerful framework for describing slow dynamics in soft-matter systems, but deriving an exact GLE for a reaction coordinate from an underlying many-body system remains generally difficult. Here, we analytically derive an exact coupled GLE for the overd…

papers.title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
papers.abstract: We present an organizing framework for concatenated quantum error correction based on the observation that the syndrome projection of a stabilizer code reshapes the noise channel in a code-determined manner. For any stabilizer code, one level of QEC maps the physical noise to a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights are fixed by the code geometry. Coherences between different syndrome classes vanish, and no physical Pauli twirl is required to reach this block-diagonal form. Concatenation can then be viewed as the iteration of the same redistribution step: the dominant logical error after one level selects the code used at the next. We instantiate the framework with the two smallest stabilizer codes, the bit-flip and phase-flip codes, and apply it to amplitude damping. The redistribution rules give the concatenation protocol $C_2(\hatσ_y) C_1(\hatσ_x)$, whose ideal-recovery fidelity scales as $f_l=1-\mathcal O(γ^2)$. Solving the crossover condition $F_l>F_{l-1}$ in the ideal-gate limit yields a critical damping parameter $γ_c\approx0.30$; in terms of the initial channel fidelity, $f=1-1.72755γ^2$. Under the same ideal-recovery assumption, we compare the overall gate accuracy rate with that of the five-qubit code. The scope of the framework, in particular for coherent and correlated noise, is stated explicitly.

papers.title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We propose distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing architecture that simultaneously exploits spatial- and spectral-domain entanglement to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges. Our scheme consists of a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers interrogating spatially separated samples, each driven by a classical frequency comb at the bright port. A single two-mode squeezed frequency comb is distributed through a passive beam-splitter array into $K$ entangled combs, establishing multipartite correlations across sensors while preserving intrinsic spectral entanglement. The protocol is compatible with both heterodyne detection and division detection, and enables parallel estimation of weighted-average absorption features over multiple frequency components. Compared with spatially separable quantum strategies requiring $K$ independently engineered nonclassical comb sources, our approach achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single quantum resource distributed across the network. These results establish a scalable route toward broadband distributed quantum spectroscopy with simultaneous spatial and spectral advantage.

papers.title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
papers.abstract: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

papers.title: Transversal syndrome extraction: A unifying construction for measuring the error syndromes of any stabilizer code
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction is fundamental to stabilizer-code-based quantum error correction, yet existing general protocols incur substantial costs in either circuit depth or width. In this work, we design ancilla stabilizer states for a general transversal circuit to construct a family of fault-tolerant syndrome-extraction gadgets that interpolate between Shor and Steane syndrome extraction for any stabilizer code. The result is a configurable trade-off between circuit depth and width.

papers.title: Discrete time liquids
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
papers.abstract: Numerically simulating quantum many-body systems is one of the central challenges in modern physics, as the exponential growth of the Hilbert space with system size renders large-scale exact solutions intractable. Over the past decade, generative artificial neural networks have emerged as powerful wave function ansätze that have powered advances in finding ground state representations, reconstructing quantum states from data, and modeling dynamics in quantum many-body systems. While recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are computationally efficient, the recurrent nature can limit their capacity to capture long-range correlations. Transformer models with their underlying self-attention mechanism excel at capturing these long-range correlations, but incur increased computational requirements, restricting applications to small physical systems. In this work, we address these limitations by exploring the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) mixer model as a wave function ansatz. By mixing information globally and locally through the system via a computationally lightweight mixing strategy, this architecture promises to combine the ability to capture long-range correlations with low computational costs. We benchmark the model on finding ground state representations of two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in various phases of matter and investigate the behavior of representational accuracy and computational efficiency for different physical system sizes. By comparing its performance to RNNs and transformer models with single-site and patched input definitions, we demonstrate that the MLP mixer architecture performs competitively with state-of-the-art network models. We further show that a hierarchical combination of this model with the transformer model outperforms other state-of-the-art architectures for large-scale quantum systems, opening new avenues for investigating quantum phases of matter.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
papers.abstract: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

papers.title: Resource Analysis of Quantum Optimization Algorithms via Variational Methods
papers.abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are promising approaches for solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices. However, the role played by quantum resources such as entanglement and coherence during the optimization process remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the evolution of these resources in two VQAs--the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON)--applied to the Minimum Vertex Cover problem. We employ a variational resource-quantification framework based on the Bures metric and Uhlmann's theorem, in which an auxiliary quantum circuit is optimized to identify the closest resource-free states. This approach allows us to quantify Bures entanglement and Bures coherence of the algorithmic states without requiring full quantum state tomography. For the considered problem instance, QAOA exhibits a pronounced accumulation of entanglement in its initial layers, followed by a progressive reduction as the algorithm converges toward the optimal solution. Its coherence likewise decreases overall with increasing circuit depth, although a finite residual value persists due to the degeneracy of the optimal-solution subspace. In contrast, FALQON exhibits a substantially lower entanglement peak, reached at larger circuit depth, followed by a decay as convergence proceeds. Its coherence decreases smoothly and monotonically together with the optimization error. These results reveal distinct quantum-resource trajectories associated with the two optimization strategies and illustrate how entanglement and coherence evolve as variational quantum states approach solutions of a classical combinatorial optimization problem.

papers.title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
papers.abstract: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons. The same educational framework was adopted for in service teacher professional development courses. Learning outcomes were evaluated through mixed methods. Preliminary analysis indicates significant improvements in conceptual understanding, confidence in using mathematical formalism, and appreciation of the relationship between theory, experimentation, and the foundations of quantum mechanics. The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.

papers.title: Data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional traffic flow model: Dimension reduction and optimization strategies
papers.abstract: We study the data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional first-order macroscopic traffic flow model, in which the movement along and across the road is described by a three-parameter flux model. The calibration is based on three real-world datasets, ranging from microscopic drone trajectories on German highways to aggregated urban sensor measurements. We recall the well-posedness of the underlying scalar conservation law and derive structural properties of the flux model. In particular, one parameter enters linearly and can be eliminated analytically, which reduces the non-linear least-squares problem from three to two dimensions. We solve the full and reduced calibration problem with two local optimization methods, Nelder-Mead and L-BFGS-B, and three global population-based methods Differential Evolution, Consensus-Based Optimization, and its deterministic variant Quasi-Monte Carlo consensus based optimization. In addition to accuracy and computational cost, we examine how sensitive the objective is to the parameters and how robust the algorithms are with respect to randomness and initialization. The reduced formulation is considerably cheaper and less sensitive to the choice of optimizer. The local methods are the most efficient when suitably initialized, whereas the global methods are more robust.

papers.abstract: While non-Markovian quantum electrodynamics has been extensively studied in the single-excitation limit, this restriction excludes the minimal nonlinear sector required to describe saturation, cascaded emission, two-photon correlations, and reservoir-mediated entanglement. In this article, we presen…
