When $N\ge3$, the same argument also recovers the classical critical existence range $0<βR<N-2$ and proves radial nondegeneracy throughout this interval. At $βR=(N-2)/2$, we exhibit $N$ linearly independent nonradial solutions of the linearized problem.

papers.title: Annealed correlation and quenched noise sensitivity in biased deep neural networks
papers.abstract: In earlier work by Jonasson, Steif and Zetterqvist (2023), fully connected deep neural networks with layers of width $n$, i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian weights, sign activations and no bias terms were shown to be annealed and quenched noise sensitive with respect to any joint probability distribution $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}$ on the input $\boldsymbolω$ and its perturbation $\boldsymbolη$ satisfying a mild positive-correlation condition and $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolη \in \{\boldsymbolω,-\boldsymbolω\}) \to 0$. Here we add independent Gaussian biases of the natural order and show that quenched noise sensitivity is retained over a broad range of depths, indeed under the slightly weaker assumption that $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolω = \boldsymbolη) \to 0$. Thus, subject to the positive-correlation condition, quenched noise sensitivity holds under the minimal requirement that the perturbed input is asymptotically unlikely to coincide with the original input. At the same time, the annealed covariance remains bounded away from zero and is entirely accounted for by fluctuations in the network-dependent output means.

papers.title: The Fer expansion of a driven spin under $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ operations cannot terminate beyond first order
papers.abstract: The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a driven quantum system as an ordered product of exponentials, each generated by the time integral of an effective Hamiltonian that governs the evolution left over by the previous factors. It can be stopped after finitely many factors whenever this leftover evolution is known in closed form, for instance when the effective Hamiltonian commutes with itself at all times, or precesses about a fixed axis with constant angular velocity. For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, in any representation, from a qubit to a spin of any size, we resum the Fer recursion into a closed map on curves in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We prove that, for a real-analytic drive, in both cases the expansion stops beyond the first factor only trivially, when the first exponential is already exact.

papers.title: Error-correction Decoding for 2D Convolutional Codes with a Generalized Viterbi Algorithm
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) convolutional codes are a generalization of one-dimensional (1D) convolutional codes and are naturally suitable for encoding two-dimensional data. Although their theoretical properties are well established, practical applications are limited due to the lack of error-correction decoding algorithms. While the Viterbi algorithm provides an efficient decoding method for 1D convolutional codes, no analogous approach exists for the 2D case. In this paper, we introduce a decoding algorithm for 2D convolutional codes, called the 2D Viterbi algorithm, extending the principles of the classical Viterbi algorithm to the two-dimensional setting. The presented 2D Viterbi algorithm works with linear systems representations of 2D convolutional codes and its complexity depends on the dimension of the corresponding 2D linear system. Hence, we also provide several algorithms to obtain 2D realizations of small dimension.

papers.title: The Great Picard theorem for quasiregular values
papers.abstract: We prove a version of Rickman's Great Picard theorem in the theory of quasiregular values. The version of the theorem that we prove is in fact stated in terms of omitted quasiregular values, unlike the previously known Little Picard theorem of the theory that is based on quasiregular values in the boundary of the image set. As a byproduct of the proof, we also prove a Riemann removability theorem in our setting, which ends up strengthening the conclusion of the previously resolved question of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin.

papers.title: A counterexample to the fractional Michael-Simon inequality
papers.abstract: We show that the fractional Michael-Simon inequality does not hold for general smooth hypersurfaces and for the range of 0 < s < (n-1)/n in the case p=1. We construct a family of smooth hypersurfaces, whose fractional mean curvature is nonnegative everywhere, which violates the inequality in the limit. The same construction yields a counterexample for every 1 \leq p < \infty for the range s < (n-1)/(np).

papers.title: Remarks on space curve $L^2$ Fourier restriction
papers.abstract: We re-examine and consider variants of the Fourier restriction theorem for space curves. In particular, we introduce a Stein--Tomas-type argument which recovers the sharp $L^2$ restriction theorem from classical oscillatory integral estimates, in the spirit of Arkhipov--Chubarikov--Karatsuba. In addition, we consider certain square function estimates which can be thought of as partial progress towards a space curve variant of the orthonormal Fourier restriction theorem of Frank--Sabin. These estimates are obtained by reducing the problem to a Kakeya-type maximal inequality, which we analyse using a formulation of the Bourgain--Guth broad/narrow method.

papers.title: The Fourier restriction problem for biradial functions
papers.abstract: We determine the exact strong-type Fourier restriction range for the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ on the class of $O(d-k)\times O(k)$-invariant functions, for every $d\geq4$ and $2\leq k\leq d-2$. This includes the critical estimates beyond the biradial Stein--Tomas endpoint left open by Mandel and Oliveira e Silva. The proof combines a weighted $L^2$ estimate for extension from a circular arc with the full two-dimensional restriction theorem. An appendix gives a direct proof of the classically conjectured range for axially symmetric functions on the whole sphere.

papers.title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.

papers.title: The Complexity of Minimal Positive Realization
papers.abstract: We study the complexity of minimal positive realization for discrete-time systems. We prove that, given a strictly proper transfer matrix with rational coefficients and an order bound encoded in unary, deciding whether a positive realization exists within that bound is complete for the existential theory of the reals. We further prove hardness for stable single-input single-output transfer functions that admit positive realizations, even when the bound equals the McMillan degree.

papers.title: Classification of SNC $(p,k)$-planes with Hodge structures of K3 type
papers.abstract: A SNC $(p,k)$-plane is a $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$-Galois cover $π\colon X \to \mathbb P^2$ with a simple normal crossing branch locus. In this setting, there exist several intermediate quotients $Y_1, Y_2,\dots, Y_{φ_{p,k}}$ corresponding to subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$ of index $p$. We focus on the case where each $Y_i$ is either a surface with geometric genus $0$ or $1$, with at least one with geometric genus $1$. We classify all SNC $(p,k)$-planes satisfying these conditions obtaining that an extensive list of cases are minimal regular surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. Moreover, these assumptions allow us to have strong control over the weight-$2$ Hodge structure of the minimal model of the covering surface $X$. Therefore, we also prove that Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures hold for such surfaces. As an independent result of our methods, we obtain a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $1$, which turn out to be precisely all K3 surfaces, and a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $0$, which turn out to be instead rational surfaces.

papers.title: Theta Relations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical quartic and cubic theta identities, we establish a product formula for Siegel--Jacobi theta series associated with rationally isometric positive-definite quadratic spaces. Our main theorem expresses a product of theta series of arbitrary Siegel degree as a finite double character sum over quotients of commensurable lattices. For the root lattice $A_2$, it yields a finite Fourier identity for cubes of cubic theta functions, a new proof of the two-variable cubic identity, and seven independent relations in degree two. A second specialization gives a new square analogue of the two-variable cubic identity. At the origin it reduces to $a(q)a(q^2)=b(q)b(q^2)+c(q)c(q^2)$; in degree two, the same seven relation patterns recur with each cube replaced by the corresponding product at $τ$ and $2τ$. We further extend the cubic identities on $A_2$ to $\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq3$, and to $2\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq2$, in arbitrary Siegel degree. The doubled-order construction recovers Jacobi's quartic identity and gives its analogues in arbitrary Siegel degree.

papers.title: Kurzweil's impulsive inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we proceed with the research initiated in (S. Antontsev \emph{et al.}, Inverse Problems, 2021). We rescale the problem in a neighbourhood $[0,1/n]$ and pass to the limit as $n$ approaches infinity. This leads to the inverse problem on an infinitesimal initial layer, which transforms the initial velocity into a new one.

papers.title: Cooling more while dissipating less: anomalous tradeoffs from thermodynamic geometry
papers.abstract: We show that, starting from the same state, optimal driving can sometimes reach a colder (or hotter) target in the same amount of time while dissipating less energy, or equivalently dissipate the same amount of energy in a shorter time. We study this counterintuitive phenomenon in the slow-driving regime of an open quantum system, where we name it Near-Equilibrium Anomalous Tradeoff (NEAT). We establish necessary conditions for its occurrence and show its underlying geometric origin. While NEAT is reminiscent of the well-known Mpemba effect, the two phenomena are distinct in general. We demonstrate NEAT in an exactly solvable qutrit model, as well as for d-dimensional birth-death dynamics with independently controlled energy levels. Finally, we show how NEAT can improve the performance of Carnot engines.

papers.title: Local-Channel Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
papers.abstract: We establish sufficient conditions for two-way local quantum-channel stability in classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells of a $d$-dimensional lattice. Each interaction multiplies the spins on the boundary of an $(m+1)$-cell. This family, defined on the full spin Hilbert space without a Gauss-law constraint, includes the Ising model at $m=0$ and the magnetic sector of the toric code at $m=1$. The low-temperature proof combines two ingredients: locally indistinguishable flat sectors and extended magnetic defects of dimension $d-m-1$. For $1\le m\le d-2$, sufficiently weak local classical perturbations at sufficiently low positive temperature preserve equivalence to the canonical flat ensemble. No internal or gauge symmetry is required of the perturbation. For weak noncommuting perturbations, we prove the same conclusion in a smaller sufficient window by reducing the diagonal probabilities to a weak classical interaction and recovering the coherences with a local channel. The conversion channels use product ancillary inputs, have polylogarithmic causal radius, and achieve any prescribed inverse-power whole-system trace-norm error. Sufficiently high-temperature states are instead two-way equivalent to a product state. Independent finite-dimensional onsite systems can be included with weak local couplings. An optimized covariance between two distant neighborhoods of parallel $m$-tori is nonincreasing under one-way local conversion and invariant under two-way conversion. Its values $\mathcal F_m=1$ and $0$ distinguish the proved low- and high-temperature domains without a protecting symmetry. These sufficient domains do not determine the full phase diagram.

papers.title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
papers.abstract: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.

papers.title: Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.

papers.title: Constant-Depth Quantum Barrier Option Pricing via a Static Bivariate Oracle Framework
papers.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation offers a theoretical quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo methods for financial derivative pricing. However, extending gate-based algorithms to path-dependent barrier options has historically been hampered by sequential path discretization, where tracking price paths across $d$ monitoring dates incurs a linear escalation in qubit footprint and gate depth ($\mathcal{O}(d)$), posing severe coherence challenges for near-term quantum processors. In this work, we present a constant-depth quantum pricing framework that fundamentally eliminates the temporal dependency of barrier monitoring. Leveraging the Brownian reflection principle and Girsanov theorem, we project the continuous supremum dynamics onto a static bivariate joint distribution of the terminal price $S_T$ and running supremum $M_T$. This allows decoupling dynamic boundary checks into a static bivariate oracle comprising two parallel comparators and a dual-controlled rotation gate. We prove this architecture reduces circuit depth and comparator complexity from $\mathcal{O}(d)$ to an invariant $\mathcal{O}(1)$, while supporting discrete monitoring via zero-quantum-cost boundary corrections. Transpilation benchmarks for daily monitoring ($d = 252$) show our framework slashes physical CNOT count by 98.59% (from 2262 to 32) and compresses two-qubit depth by 98.02% (from 1514 to 30 layers). Under a realistic 127-qubit IBM Eagle noise model, the shallow circuit achieves a 7.84% relative valuation error with M3 readout mitigation. Finally, the framework seamlessly extends to nonlinear exotic payoffs lacking analytical solutions, establishing a noise-resilient pathway toward practical quantum advantage in computational finance.

papers.title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, ρ)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.

papers.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.

papers.title: Schrödinger estimates with arbitrarily small periodic regularity on $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{T}$
papers.abstract: Let $M=\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{T}$ carry its product metric. We prove that the Schrödinger evolution maps $L^2(\mathbb{H}^2;H^s(\mathbb{T}))$ into $L^2([0,1];L^6(M))$ for every $s>0$, without any regularity assumption in the hyperbolic variable. The proof separates hyperbolic and periodic frequencies. A localized hyperbolic kernel estimate restricts the effective interaction time at hyperbolic frequency $L$ to order $L^{-1}$. Quadratic exponential sums then give a logarithmic bound when the periodic bandwidth is comparable to $L$. A mixed-norm decoupling argument, including an $L^6$-valued extension and a periodic transference step, reduces wider periodic bands to this case. The infimum of the admissible periodic regularities is therefore zero. The estimate at zero regularity is not established here.

papers.title: Rational analytic prismatization
papers.abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory

papers.title: On the Fluctuations of Associated Primes and Depths of Powers of Monomial Ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the fluctuation phenomenon in the sets of associated primes and depths of powers of monomial ideals. We provide affirmative answers to two open questions posed in [8] concerning the existence of monomial ideals in K[x,y,z] whose associated primes exhibit prescribed patterns of appearance, disappearance, and reappearance of the maximal ideal across specified ranges of powers. For each construction, we also derive the corresponding fluctuation in depths. Furthermore, we construct a square-free monomial ideal that is nearly normally torsion-free but fails to satisfy the persistence property, thereby answering a question posed in [20] in the negative. This example arises as the edge ideal of the ideal minimally non-packing clutter Q_10, revealing an intriguing connection between combinatorial optimization and the algebraic properties of monomial ideals.

papers.title: Sparse block encoding with low subnormalisation for quantum linear solvers on unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: Unstructured meshes are widely used in modelling and simulation in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) due to their geometric flexibility. However, they require an efficient block encoding circuit describing the system. Here, we present a new block encoding methodology for unstructured mesh solvers based on decomposing the system matrix into a sum of 1-sparse matrices. This block encoding is engineered to reduce subnormalisation even in the absence of structure by hiding the contribution of large matrix elements behind others. We investigate three methods of 1-sparse decomposition. Our circuit constructions can optionally take advantage of limited matrix bandwidth and repeated values. For example we consider digitisation (reduced precision), where the number of multiplexed rotation gates is equal to the number of non-unique matrix entries. We evaluate our methodologies using 2D and 3D CFD matrices for unstructured aerofoil meshes, structured cavity, and duct meshes, with and without matrix preconditioning. Our results show that we are able to achieve a block encoding with a near constant subnormalisation factor as the number of matrix preconditioning infill levels increases. This significantly reduces the subnormalised condition number and, in one case, reduces the degree of the QSP polynomial approximation to $1/x$ by 100,000. Reduced precision digitisation is shown to become more effective as the number of preconditioning infill levels is increased and, in one case, reduces the number of multiplexed rotations from 2,785,576 to 546 whilst maintaining an infidelity of $2.6\times10^{-5}$ relative to the classical solution. The effect of digitisation on QSVT solutions is demonstrated using 2D and 3D unstructured mesh aerofoil cases. Due to its flexibility and automatic applicability, we believe our 1-sparse decomposition block encoding can offer benefits to other quantum applications.

papers.title: U-Examples: A Unified Family of Worst-Case Instances for Optimization Algorithms
papers.abstract: Worst-case instances show where optimization algorithms fail: the Klee-Minty cube for the simplex method, ill-conditioned and rippled bowls for gradient descent, degenerate minima for Newton's method, redundant Klee-Minty cubes for interior-point methods, unprunable trees for branch-and-bound, deceptive landscapes for metaheuristics, and degenerate cycling for active-set methods. These constructions were developed over seventy years in separate literatures, each with its own tools. This survey reviews them together. We trace the history of rule-specific worst cases across seven representative algorithm classes and organize them with one reading: in each, the optimum lies near the start, yet the algorithm's own update rule is misdirected onto a long trajectory or, at the boundary, into a non-terminating loop. We call such an instance a U-Example; the letter U stands both for the unification and for the U-shaped bowls around which descent methods are made to crawl. A common framework treats every algorithm as a rule on a state space with a progress potential, so that one definition of misdirection, and of the resulting blow-up in cost, covers pivoting, descent, interior-point, tree-search, and population methods. Each member is drawn in a common visual grammar and quantified in general dimension $n$. The blow-up is independent of the dimension for the two descent members and exponential in it for four search members, with degenerate cycling as a breakdown. We connect the constructions to neighbouring theories (oracle complexity, performance estimation, smoothed analysis, and the complexity of local search), each of which asks a different question of the same instances. We then map each worst case to the remedy that defeats it, examine how robust the instances are, and close with open challenges, in particular whether a worst case can be predicted from the update rule alone.

papers.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
papers.abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

papers.title: An Aldous-type tightness characterisation for the $M_1$ topology: replacing global modulus control by local control at stopping times
papers.abstract: Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

papers.title: The Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture for the Fisher-KPP equation
papers.abstract: We resolve the Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture, which concerns the classification of all [0,1]-valued entire solutions of Fisher-KPP equations with concave C^2 reaction terms in arbitrary space dimension. We prove that every such solution is a C_{loc}^{1,2} limit of solutions generated by finitely many planar traveling fronts, possibly together with a spatially homogeneous solution. Our approach reveals an ordered linear structure underlying the nonlinear solution space, leading to a critical-subcritical spectral decomposition. The proof combines linear reconstruction of subcritical approximants with a measure representation (a kind of nonlinear Martin representation) of critical solutions, obtained through small-amplitude asymptotics and comparison with a radially symmetric entire solution.

papers.title: Stability and instability for particle dynamics in magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We study zero-speed equilibria of the Newton-Lorentz equation $\ddot x=\dot x\times B(x)$ in $\mathbf{R}^3$, which describes the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field $B$. We prove Lyapunov instability wherever the field $B$ does not vanish (under $C^1$ regularity), and at every isolated zero of $B$ provided it is real-analytic. These results do not assume that the field is divergence-free. In contrast, we construct a compactly supported divergence-free $C^\infty$ field that is flat at an isolated zero and makes the corresponding equilibrium Lyapunov stable.

papers.title: Almost entropic matroids and $(k,L)$-systems
papers.abstract: For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.

papers.title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. Numerical optimization involving stiff evolutionary and static PDEs often requires solving a large system of equations, which can be treated as a constraint. In this work, we present a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver that incorporates this constraint. We evaluate its performance across four key tasks: a) linear and nonlinear forward modeling of evolutionary and static problems, b) solving inverse problems to estimate equation coefficients, c) solving inverse problems to estimate the right-hand side, and d) learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. These capabilities make it a powerful tool for different physics and engineering applications, in particular for geophysics, where inverse problems are commonly solved in order to reduce the model uncertainty.

papers.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
papers.abstract: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $α> 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+α^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-Hörmander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $α$, so that on the band $-α^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $α$.

papers.title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
papers.abstract: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.

papers.title: Classification of positive solutions to the critical Lane-Emden system
papers.abstract: We classify all positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system $$ -Δu=v^p \, \, \text{in } \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, \, \, -Δv=u^q \, \, \text{in} \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $N\geq3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy $$ \frac{1}{p+1}+\frac{1}{q+1}=\frac{N-2}{N}.$$Without assuming boundedness, decay at infinity, or finite energy, we prove that every such solution has the form $$ u(x)=λ^{\frac{N}{q+1}}U(λ(x-a)), \, \, v(x)=λ^{\frac{N}{p+1}}V(λ(x-a)), $$ for some $a\in \mathbb{R}^N$ and $λ>0$, where $(U,V)$ is the positive radial ground state centered at the origin and normalized by $U(0)=1$. Consequently, both components are radially symmetric about the same point and satisfy $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}u^{q+1}\, dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}v^{p+1}\,dx<\infty. $$ Our result extends the classical classification of positive solutions of the critical Sobolev equation by Caffarelli, Gidas and Spruck and Chen and Li to the critical Lane-Emden system.

papers.title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
papers.abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.

papers.title: Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the following inverse domain uncertainty quantification problem: given a prescribed value or measurement of a hemodynamic biomarker, characterize the distribution of vascular geometries compatible with it. The problem is formulated as a Bayesian inverse problem in which a high-dimensional latent parameter encodes the cardiovascular shape and accounts for inter-patient variability. The parameter-to-observable map composes a conditional LDDMM stochastic interpolant generating the aortic surface with a high-performance numerical finite element solver for the unsteady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations, from which biomarkers of interest are evaluated. The map is nonlinear, high-dimensional and computationally expensive. To address the problem, we compare three ensemble strategies: ensemble adjusted Kalman inversion (EAKI), adaptive Bayesian updating with structural reliability (aBUS), and a Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) sequential Monte Carlo scheme. The first two approaches are derivative-free. For the third method, we introduce a novel differentiable flow-matching surrogate that reduces the cost of a single forward map evaluation at the price of a distribution shift depending on the training distribution used for the surrogate. We apply the framework to the generation of virtual patient cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops along aortic geometries affected by coarctation, and we validate and compare the three methods on synthetic data.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Scheme for Computing the Gradient of the Eikonal Equation
papers.abstract: We propose a first-order, structure-preserving method for directly computing the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation in smooth first-arrival regions. The method combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) in a Godunov-type upwind discretization with spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration. This construction gives a tangent residual and keeps every iterate on $\mathbb{S}^2$ without projection or normalization. The SLERP discretization exactly preserves a family of curved orientation equilibria. Removing the background discretization bias improves absolute orientation accuracy near these equilibria, allowing a prescribed error tolerance to be reached on a coarser grid. We prove the equilibrium-preservation property and, separately, a smaller angular error for SFE than normalized Euler in a one-cell relaxation under the stated step-size condition. Two- and three-dimensional experiments examine convergence, geometric preservation, and computational cost. Comparisons with gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes show more accurate directions on the same grid in the curved media considered. The method provides direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential use in adjoint-based inverse problems.

papers.title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
papers.abstract: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.

papers.title: Front-pinned spectral collocation for the flame problem and related ignition problems
papers.abstract: We consider global Chebyshev collocation for the ignition problems $y'=y^q(1-y)$, $y(0)=δ$, $q\ge2$; for $q=2$ this is the flame problem, a standard stiff test equation. After rescaling to $[-1,1]$ the solution has an interior layer of width $O(μ)$, $μ=(q-1)δ^{q-1}$, at a $δ$-dependent position. Two obstacles arise: plain Chebyshev collocation needs $O(1/μ)$ nodes, and imposing the initial condition amplifies errors by a factor of order $1/μ$, which makes the collocation equations severely ill-conditioned. Our main contribution addresses the second one. Since all solutions are translates of one profile, the initial condition can be replaced by an equivalent interior condition. For an unknown $u=\varphi(y)$, imposing it where the speed $|\varphi'f_q|$ of $u$ along the orbit is maximal bounds the propagator of the linearized equation by one; for $u=\ln y$ this is $y(x^\ast)=(q-1)/q$. For the first obstacle we use the sinh map of Tee and Trefethen: the time function is explicit, the complex singularities of the profile lie exactly at $\pm(2k+1)πi$, and the map parameters follow in closed form, so that $O(\ln(1/μ))$ nodes suffice. In double precision the pinned scheme reaches the interpolation error of the exact solution in five or six Newton iterations for $μ$ down to $10^{-12}$, whereas the initial-condition form fails or converges to wrong discrete solutions, also in an integral (Birkhoff) reformulation. Computations in $256$-bit arithmetic confirm the predicted rate down to errors of $10^{-70}$, AAA approximation locates the singularities to within $2\%$, and the method carries over to an Arrhenius reaction rate, with all parameters computed numerically.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorems for Optimal Transport Functionals
papers.abstract: We establish central limit theorems for empirical plug-in estimators of scalar functionals of quadratic optimal transport maps and potentials, including Wasserstein costs and several risk measures constructed from transport-based multivariate quantiles. We study the one-sample problem with a known reference distribution and i.i.d. observations from the target distribution. A natural approach is to combine a limit theorem for the empirical transport map with the functional delta method. We show, however, that in dimensions at least two, empirical transport-map errors admit no nonzero weak limit in $L^2$ under any normalizing scale. Instead, we linearize the functional directly in the target distribution, obtaining an influence-function expansion with a remainder controlled by the transport-map error. The influence function is characterized by a linear elliptic partial differential equation. Under regularity conditions, we use this expansion to prove central limit theorems in low dimensions and establish validity of the empirical bootstrap. We also derive semiparametric efficiency bounds and show that the plug-in estimators attain them under the same conditions.

papers.title: Atmospheric channel model for QKD over satellite megaconstellations
papers.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. The model is validated with available data from missions such as Micius and Hispasat, including a secondary viability assessment for a hypothetical Starlink-based quantum communication network, where we evaluate the predicted channel behavior in terms of single-photon transmittance and power balance, alongside the channel capacity of the link for uplink and downlink exclusively. Our comparative analysis demonstrates the ability of our channel model to predict real data under simple atmospheric behavior assumptions, which offer practical guidelines for the design and optimization of future quantum satellite missions.

papers.title: Plasticity of the unit sphere of the space $c_0$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the unit sphere of the space $c_{0}$ is plastic, i.e., every non-expansive bijection from this sphere onto itself is an isometry.

papers.title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
papers.abstract: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

papers.title: The Lévy-Khinchine type representations and generalized functions on Bernstein spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the class of all univariate probability laws whose characteristic functions do not have zeroes on the real line. This class contains the fundamental family of infinitely divisible distributions and its new extension, the set of rational-(quasi-)infinitely divisible laws. We prove that this class is dense in the family of all probability laws with respect to the total variation distance. We show that characteristic functions corresponding to this class admit Lévy-Khinchine type representations. In these formulas, the generalized spectral functions (the regularized Lévy measures) are special continuous linear functionals on the union of well known Bernstein spaces of entire functions of exponential type which are additionally bounded on the real line. We apply this spectral functions in criteria of weak convergence of distributions within the class under study. All necessary analytical constructions are proposed.

papers.title: Finite groups with large sum of element orders compared to cyclic groups
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$ let $ψ(G)$ denote the sum of the orders of elements in $G$. If $G$ has order $n$ then, by a result of Amiri, Jafarian Amiri and Isaacs, $ψ(G)\leψ(C_n)$, where $C_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. We determine all finite groups such that $ψ(G)\ge\frac{1}{3}ψ(C_n)$.

papers.title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.

papers.title: Beta-expansions induced by general Parry polynomials and sharp iteration asymptotics of their transfer operators
papers.abstract: This paper generalizes previous results to any Parry polynomials $p_n(z)$ \cite{Pa} of finite degree $n\geq 2$. Let $β>1$ be the unique positive root of $p_n$ and consider the transfer operator $\mathscr{P}$ induced by the map $[0,1]\ni x\mapsto βx-\lfloor βx\rfloor \in [0,1)$. Suppose all other roots of $p_n$ have magnitude less than one. Then for any smooth function $F$ on $[0,1]$ we prove two term asymptotics in $L^\infty$ of the form \begin{equation*} \big(\mathscr{P}^r(F)\big)(\cdot)= u(\cdot) \int_0^1 F(x)\: \mathrm{d} x +β^{-r}v(\cdot) \big (F(1)-F(0)\big )+o(β^{-r}),\quad r\geq 1, \end{equation*} where $u$ is piecewise constant and $\mathscr{P}u=u$, while $v$ is piecewise equal to a polynomial of degree one and $\mathscr{P}v= β^{-1}v$. When $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to functions of bounded variation $BV([0,1])$, it is known that $\vert z \vert\leq β^{-1}$ contains its essential spectrum. Thus the contribution coming from $v$ in the above estimate is not guaranteed if $F$ is not smooth enough. Furthermore, we show that when $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to $BV([0,1])$ then any $\vert z \vert<β^{-1}$ is an eigenvalue with infinite multiplicity. Moreover, we construct a meromorphic extension of $(\mathscr{P}-z)^{-1}$ to the domain $\vert z \vert>β^{-1}$, where the finite rank poles are numbers $ζ$ with $β^{-1}<\vert ζ\vert\leq 1$ such that $βζ$ is a root of $p_n(z)$. If such poles $ζ$ other than $1$ exist, then we construct eigenvectors of $\mathscr{P}^*$ in $BV^*$ obeying $\mathscr{P}^*\hat{U}=ζ\hat{U}$, where $\hat{U}(F)$ is given by series involving the values of $F$ taken in some specially chosen, finer and finer partitions of $[0,1]$. When $F$ is either a polynomial or a characteristic function like $χ_{[0,x]}$, then $\hat{U}(F)$ can be explicitly computed.

papers.title: Payoff Polarization and Garbage Concentration in a Stochastic Garbage Disposal Game
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic garbage disposal game on a finite graph in which agents transfer garbage through pairwise interactions governed by payoff-dependent Fermi probabilities. We investigate the long-term behavior of both payoffs and garbage distributions. We prove that payoff dispersion grows at least linearly in time almost surely, leading to payoff polarization, with the maximum and minimum payoffs diverging to positive and negative infinity, respectively. Moreover, the payoff range grows at least on the order of the square root of time. For garbage dynamics, we establish almost-sure concentration on a single agent in the two-agent case for any positive disposal efficiency. When disposal is complete and the underlying graph is connected, we further prove that all garbage becomes concentrated on a single agent after a finite random time, although the agent holding the garbage may change over time. These results characterize the emergence of payoff inequality and garbage concentration in stochastic competitive interactions on networks.

papers.title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
papers.abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. However, the method usually leads to ill-conditioned linear systems with a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), limiting its application. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.

papers.title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
papers.abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for quantum information processing. In transmon circuits, higher excited states provide additional pathways for engineering interactions within the computational subspace. Here we demonstrate controlled-Z (CZ) gates that exploit two noncomputational states, $\ket{02}$ and $\ket{20}$, through selective Floquet coupling. The nontrivial parametric modulation can activate both auxiliary transitions from $\ket{11}$ while suppressing the leading exchange between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$. Based on this approach, we develop two gate protocols: a nonadiabatic round trip through a bright auxiliary superposition and adiabatic evolution along a zero-energy dark state, both achieving average gate fidelities above $99.99\%$ in numerical simulations. Control of the modulation phase further extends the bright-state protocol to conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates. Effective-model simulations show that unconventional control improves tolerance to residual $ZZ$ coupling and static qubit-frequency offsets relative to conventional control over the parameter ranges examined. Simulations including neighboring spectator qubits show that the original nonadiabatic bright-state and adiabatic dark-state CZ protocols retain high gate fidelities. This framework offers new routes toward the experimental realization of CZ gates and their geometric implementations.

papers.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $μ$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.

papers.title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity of smooth polytopes with few facets
papers.abstract: For each dimension $d$, we determine the minimum number of facets of a smooth $d$-dimensional lattice polytope whose Ehrhart polynomial has at least one negative coefficient. This minimum is six in dimension $d=3$, seven in dimension $d=4$, and $d+2$ in every dimension $d\ge 5$. The lower bounds follow from the classification of smooth lattice polytopes with at most $d+2$ facets, together with explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials in dimensions at most $4$. We also prove that a lattice polytope of dimension at least $3$ with a smooth vertex cannot be $2$-integral with respect to any ordered lattice basis.

papers.title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

papers.title: The Dimension Landscape of Bivariate $C^2$ Splines
papers.abstract: Schumaker's lower bound incorporates local geometric corrections and provides insight into the dimensions of bivariate spline spaces. Building on this bound, we study bivariate $C^2$ spline dimensions from three perspectives: universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps. We prove universal attainment in degree seven for every legal realization of every triangulation. We prove generic attainment in degrees five and six for every fixed combinatorial triangulation and give explicit polynomial conditions certifying generic failure on fixed triangulations in degrees three and four. For geometric jumps with matching local direction types at corresponding interior vertices, we prove nonexistence in degree seven and construct examples in degrees three and five. In degree six, universal attainment and the existence of such geometric jumps remain open questions.

papers.title: Non-null ruled surfaces and pseudo hyper-dual tangent sphere bundles
papers.abstract: In this paper, the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres are defined. Then, a new family of non-null ruled surfaces associated with hyper-dual Lorentzian curves is defined via the E.Study hyper-map in Minkowski space and the definitions of the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres. Within this framework, the resulting non-null ruled surfaces are classified. Necessary and sufficient conditions for developability are obtained with their geometric interpretations in terms of hyper-dual Lorentzian curves and arc-length parameters. Moreover, explicit examples are presented to verify the theoretical results.

papers.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
papers.abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindelöf-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

papers.title: The strong type endpoint estimate for the local spherical maximal function
papers.abstract: Let $p_d=(d^2+1)/(d(d-1))$ and $q_d=(d^2+1)/(d-1)$. We prove that the local spherical maximal operator $\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2}|f*dσ_t|$ is bounded from $L^{p_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L^{q_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $d\geq 2$. Previously only the restricted weak type estimate was known at this endpoint. Together with known results, this completes the characterization of the strong type $L^p\to L^q$ bounds for the local spherical maximal operator. We also prove the maximal estimate \[ \Big\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|e^{it\sqrt{-Δ}}f|\Big\|_{L^{2(d+1)/(d-1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \lesssim\|f\|_{\dot H^{d/(d+1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \] for the wave equation at the critical exponent. Both results are obtained by exploiting the gain in bilinear estimates that comes from the interaction between high and low frequencies.

papers.title: New Directions in Irrationality
papers.abstract: Since Apéry's proof of the irrationality of $ζ(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Apéry as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $μ(ζ(2))<4.62675$ and $μ(ζ(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,ζ(3),ζ(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $μ(Aζ(3)+Bζ(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.

papers.title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
papers.abstract: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

papers.title: Absolute winning properties of exceptional sets for rational maps
papers.abstract: We study Schmidt's game on the Julia set $J(f)$ of weak hyperbolic rational maps $f:\CC\to\CC$. For each $y\in J(f)$, let $E(f,y)$ be the set of points in $J(f)$ whose forward orbits stay a positive distance from $y$. We prove that $E(f,y)$ is absolute winning on $J(f)$ for each $y \in J(f)$. To do this, we first prove the absolute winning property for the exceptional set associated to the critical points by a potential game argument, and then use uniform expansion to obtain the result for each target point $y$.

papers.title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium. After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level $Λ$ system. This spectral narrowing is associated with the decreasing separation between the two inner dressed states as atomic velocity increases. The transparency window exhibits pronounced direction-dependent transmission, with high forward transmission and strong suppression in the reverse direction. The transparency linewidth and forward-backward probe transmission can be controlled via two independent driving fields, while the central transparency frequency is kept essentially unchanged. The resulting narrowband nonreciprocity supports high forward transmission together with strong suppression in the reverse direction, which is suitable for frequency-selective optical filtering and nonreciprocal optical transmission in thermal atomic media. Our scheme with these specific features is geared towards enabling compact vapor-cell-based nonreciprocal devices for quantum network applications.

papers.title: Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions
papers.abstract: For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $ω(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leqω(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.

papers.title: Size and spectral radius conditions for the existence of $k$-factor in graphs with given minimum degree
papers.abstract: In recent years, characterizing the conditions for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in graphs has received significant academic attention. For integers $b\ge a\ge 1$, an $[a, b]$-factor of a graph $G$ is defined as a spanning subgraph $H$ such that $a\le d_{H}(v)\le b$ for every $v\in V(G)$. If $a=b=k$, a $[k, k]$-factor is called a $k$-factor of $G$. Let $δ(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. Hao and Li [Electron. J. Combin. (2024)] posed the problem of characterizing the size or spectral radius conditions for a graph to contain an $[a,b]$-factor with $δ(G)\ge a$. Fan, Lin and Zhu [Discrete Math. (2026)] solved the size version of this problem for the case $a < b.$ In this paper, for $a=b=k$, we characterize the size condition for a graph to have a $k$-factor with $δ(G)\ge k$. Using this result, we also characterize the spectral radius and distance spectral radius conditions for a graph to have a $k$-factor, respectively.

papers.title: Fates of Exact Finite-$N$ First-Order Transitions: Coherent Suppression versus Spectral-Collapse Termination
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected ground-state crossings can produce exact first-order transitions (FOTs) even at finite $N$, in contrast to continuous transitions governed by soft-mode criticality. We establish exact Juddian ground-state crossings for arbitrary finite $N$ in the one- and two-photon anisotropic Dicke models and identify a common two-channel structure: the eigenvalues of the coupling matrix set the local normal-state instability thresholds, whereas its determinant fixes the exact crossing. Despite this common structure, the resulting FOTs have distinct fates determined by the bosonic response. In the one-photon model, the overlap between coherent Juddian branches vanishes in the thermodynamic or infinite frequency-ratio limits, asymptotically suppressing the FOT cusp. In the two-photon model, squeezed Juddian states lose normalizability at spectral collapse, thereby terminating the physical FOT line at finite $N$. Although the cusp strength tends to zero as the endpoint is approached, the terminating FOT retains a collective spectral signature: the different-parity gap is predicted to close with an $N$-dependent exponent $μ_N=(2N+3)/4$, one greater than the cusp termination exponent. By contrast, the same-parity soft mode retains $N$-independent square-root scaling and governs the critical response. Thus spectral collapse can terminate an exact finite-$N$ FOT while preserving its collective imprint in the parity-resolved spectrum.

papers.title: Orbital stability of standing waves for defocusing fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equations with a delta potential
papers.abstract: In this paper, a fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a delta potential and a repulsive nonlinearity in one space dimension is considered. First, it is proved that the Cauchy problem in Sobolev spaces on the real line is globally well-posed, independently of the sign of the delta potential. Moreover, in the case of an attractive delta potential, the existence, the minimization properties and the orbital stability of standing waves under the flow of the equation are established. The stability proof is based on concentration-compactness methods for the energy/charge functional. For that purpose, no explicit calculation of the standing waves is required and the results are based on the variational properties of the solutions alone.

papers.title: Bidirectional Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation of Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: We propose an approximate classical algorithm for estimating quantum circuits' transition amplitudes, $\langle Ψ_f | \hat{U} | Ψ_0 \rangle$, based on Monte Carlo sums over bidirectionally sampled Feynman paths. The algorithm generates Feynman paths, i.e., sequences of intermediate computational basis states, by combining information from random walks initiated at both the input and output states, $Ψ_0$ and $Ψ_f$, respectively. It further combines this bidirectional approach with Multiple Importance Sampling, a powerful variance reduction technique that avoids variance peaks caused by divisions by the very low sampling probabilities associated with hard to reach paths. Empirical data demonstrate the superior convergence rate exhibited by the bidirectional algorithm over a unidirectional, forward-only sampling approach. This superiority is due to the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in finding and weighting paths with non-zero amplitude in an extremely sparse path space. Sum of paths algorithms exhibit very favourable space complexity. Monte Carlo replaces exhaustive enumeration of the exponentially large path space by stochastic sampling, the computational cost being determined by the variance of the estimator. This work demonstrates these two features by presenting results on very large quantum circuits, with up to 4096 qubits.

papers.title: A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
papers.abstract: We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.

papers.title: Control variates for dry friction under colored noise: variance rates for non-smooth observables
papers.abstract: A control variate method was introduced by Garnier and Mertz (2022) for multivalued stochastic differential equations driven by colored noise. For smooth observables, the asymptotic variance is $O(\varepsilon^{2})$, where $\varepsilon^{2}$ is the correlation time of the noise. However, for non-smooth reliability observables, such as threshold indicators and overshoot severities, rate estimates have not been established in general. In this paper, rate estimates are derived for the inertial dry-friction inclusion driven by colored noise in the three regimes whose white-noise propagators are known. The asymptotic variance of the resulting control variate estimators is $O(\varepsilon^{2α})$ for $α$-Hölder observables with $α\in(0,1]$, $O(\varepsilon)$ for observables of bounded variation satisfying a one-sided continuity condition, $O(\varepsilon^{1+α})$ for observables that are both $α$-Hölder and of bounded variation, and $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{2,1+2α\}})$ for observables with finitely many $α$-cusps, where $α\in (0, 1]$ is the cusp exponent. The last three bounds hold up to logarithmic factors. Bounds on the bias of the white-noise approximation and non-asymptotic sample-size estimates are also derived, and the comparison principle is shown to be preserved under coupled time discretization. Numerical experiments in the three regimes support the predicted rates.

papers.title: Searching for Axion Dark Matter via Superconductor-Spin Hybrid Magnetometers
papers.abstract: Axions are a compelling dark matter candidate suggested by theories beyond the Standard Model. The predicted axion-electron coupling and the resulting pseudomagnetic field allow for laboratory axion searches. Here we report an experimental axion search via a superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer. A state-of-the-art broadband magnetometer with a sensitivity of sub-100 aT/Hz$^{1/2}$ at tens of kHz has been realized by coupling a ferrite spin sensor to a readout system based on a superconducting quantum interference device. The most stringent terrestrial constraints on the axion-electron coupling have been established in the frequency range 5$\sim$60 kHz. In the future, an improvement on the constraints of more than 4 orders of magnitude is foreseeable through arrays of superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometers with optimized designs. This work demonstrates the potential of superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometers in high-precision magnetic field sensing and the study of fundamental physics.

papers.title: Bulk limits of the truncated circular beta ensembles
papers.abstract: We study the bulk limits of the rank-one truncation of the circular beta ensembles obtained by deleting the first row and column. We prove that the normalized Blaschke products of the truncated circular beta ensembles converge in law to a constant multiple (depending on $β$) of the i.i.d.~Gaussian analytic function (GAF) uniformly on compacts of the unit disk. As a consequence, we identify the bulk point process limit with the zero set of GAF, which was proved in the seminal work of Peres and Virág to form a determinantal point process with the Bergman kernel. Our method also applies to the rank-one multiplicative perturbations of the circular beta ensembles in the mesoscopic regime.

papers.title: Spectral analysis of multi-bubble solutions to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
papers.abstract: We investigate weighted spectral limits for separated multi-bubble configurations and refined spectral asymptotics for the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[ -Δu=u^p+\varepsilon u^q, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$ with $N\geq3$, $p=(N+2)/(N-2)$, $1\leq q<p$ and $\varepsilon$ is a positive parameter. We first determine the limits of the ordered weighted eigenvalues associated with families of positive functions admitting an $m$-bubble decomposition at distinct interior points with a remainder vanishing in $H_0^1(Ω)$. The limiting eigenvalues are those of the single-bubble problem, with all multiplicities multiplied by $m$. We then refine this analysis for positive multi-bubble solutions of this problem with comparable concentration scales, deriving precise expansions of the first $(N+2)m$ eigenvalues and characterizing their eigenfunctions when $1<q<3$ if $N=4$ or $1\leq q<p$ if $N\geq5$. The leading corrections are determined by explicit symmetric matrices involving $q$, the concentration parameters, and the Green and Robin functions. In particular, we prove that the dilation matrix is positive definite. Together, these spectral results yield Morse index bounds for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, with an exact formula when the matrix governing the translation modes is invertible.

papers.title: Constant Step Sizes for Muon-Type Spectral Optimizers on Strongly Convex Quadratics
papers.abstract: Muon and related optimizers update a weight matrix with a spectrally transformed gradient. In this work, we study such spectral optimizers with a constant step size on strongly convex matrix quadratics, which isolate the effect of the update from the confounds of nonconvexity, noise, and step size schedules. We analyze an update using two quantities: the gain, which is the factor by which it amplifies the gradient along each singular direction, and the length, which is the norm of the update. These two quantities place the popular spectral updates in three regimes with different behavior: (i) with a bounded gain, the iterates behave like preconditioned gradient descent and converge for step sizes set by the largest curvature; (ii) with an unbounded gain but a vanishing length, they still converge, with the admissible step sizes set by the total curvature instead; and (iii) with a non-vanishing length, they do not converge for almost every initialization. Interestingly, the practical variants of Muon fall in all three regimes, depending only on how the update is normalized and scaled and not on the polynomial that approximates the polar factor. Experiments validate these findings.

papers.title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
papers.abstract: We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs. Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internal idler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm. In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale. Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.

papers.title: Eliminating the Higgs field and perturbing Yang-Mills connections in cone Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We study the configurations of the cone Yang-Mills functional over a closed connected manifold. We show that the Euler-Lagrange equation from variations in the Higgs field is always uniquely solvable for $ζ\neq 0$, allowing us to eliminate one of the two equations from the theory. By eliminating the equation, we obtain a family of ``effective cone Yang-Mills functionals'' on the space of connection 1-forms indexed by $ζ$, which reduce to Yang-Mills theory when $ζ= 0$. This suggests a way to nontrivially deform the Yang-Mills moduli space. We take the first step towards this deformation by showing that, near certain critical points of the Yang-Mills functional, there is a family of smooth connections $A_t$ which satisfy the $tζ$-cone Yang-Mills equations.

papers.title: Sharp boundedness criteria for nonnegative kernels on regular curves in the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: In this paper we study singular integrals associated with the nonnegative kernels \[ K_α(x,y,z)=\frac{|z|^{α/2}}{\|(x,y,z)\|^{α+1}}, \qquad α>0, \] in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb H$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Korányi norm. This family was introduced by Chousionis and Li. We first show that there exists a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve $E\subset\mathbb H$ such that the singular integrals associated with $K_α$ are unbounded on $L^2(E)$ for every $0<α<4$. This extends the counterexamples of Chousionis, Li and Zhang from $0<α<2$ to the full range $0<α<4$. Combined with the boundedness theorem of Fässler and Orponen for $α\ge4$, our result determines the exact range of exponents for boundedness on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve. We also consider the more general kernels \[ K_Φ(p)=\frac{1}{\|p\|} Φ\!\left(\frac{|z|^{1/2}}{\|p\|}\right), \qquad p=(x,y,z)\neq0, \] where $Φ:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $Φ(0)=0$. We show that the associated singular integral is $L^2$-bounded on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve if and only if $Φ(u)=O(u^4)$ as $u\to0$. When this condition fails, we construct a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve on which the operator is unbounded.
