The curves in both constructions can be chosen as horizontal lifts of planar $C^1$ graphs with arbitrarily small slope.

papers.title: Axion detection in the non-Markovian noise
papers.abstract: The detection of axion dark matter poses a significant challenge due to its exceptionally weak coupling to standard-model particles. Here we develop a noise-tolerant quantum-metrology scheme based on coupled $^{129}$Xe spin ensembles to search for such weakly interacting particles. Within an experimentally accessible parameter regime, our scheme achieves an ideal exclusion limit on the axion coupling constant that is several orders of magnitude more stringent than that of conventional detection methods. We further investigate the performance of our scheme under dissipative noise and find that its robustness is fundamentally governed by the energy-spectrum structure of the composite spin-environment system. Remarkably, when a bound state emerges in the spectrum, the exclusion limit asymptotically recovers its ideal value in the non-Markovian dynamics, whereas under the Markovian approximation the limit deteriorates significantly due to noise. Our results establish a universal mechanism for noise-resilient exploration of beyond-standard-model physics, which can be practically implemented by engineering bound-state formation via tuning the Larmor frequency of the spin ensembles.

papers.title: Forest Characterization of When SDP-RLT Strengthens RLT for Bilinear Terms
papers.abstract: We study two relaxations for bilinear terms in box-constrained variables: the reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) relaxation and the SDP-RLT relaxation, which combines RLT with semidefinite programming (SDP). We represent the pattern of bilinear terms by an undirected graph, with one vertex for each variable and one edge for each bilinear term. A point feasible for the RLT relaxation fixes only part of the lifted matrix of the SDP-RLT relaxation, leaving the remaining entries to be chosen subject to the diagonal RLT inequalities, and the two relaxations differ exactly when these entries cannot always be chosen so that the matrix becomes positive semidefinite. Formulating this as a positive semidefinite matrix completion problem, we show that the feasible regions of the two relaxations coincide if and only if the graph is a forest. We also measure how large the difference can be when the graph contains a complete bipartite subgraph: a bilinear objective given by a Hadamard matrix yields optimal values whose ratio grows with the size of that subgraph.

papers.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
papers.abstract: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both constructed from the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. The first consists of affine moments of ordinary powers. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<β<1$, we prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity in the polynomial variable by a continuant comparison criterion. We also determine leading continuants, Hankel determinants, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. The second deformation uses Askey--Wilson basis products and yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel. We give two independent moment evaluations and prove that its row polynomials have simple negative zeros and are $γ$-positive after palindromic normalization. An Askey--Wilson integral with base $q^2$ gives a continuous-parameter extension and a moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion, including its integrality. An ordinary-power expansion also proves Pan's Touchard identity. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $θ>-1$, we prove total positivity of the kernel triangle by a Jackson $q$-Bessel--Edrei factorization and strict total positivity of its associated square by a discrete moment representation. This gives a simultaneous $(θ,q)$-extension of Wang--Yang's theorems for type $A$ and type $B$ Narayana triangles and squares. We further establish coefficientwise total nonnegativity in $q$ through order two for the endpoint triangles. An exact triangular change of basis links the two deformations and explains their common classical limit.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
papers.abstract: Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/runtime-barrier-monitor.

papers.title: Lattice Moduli and Residual Atoms
papers.abstract: We study prescribed holomorphic lattices for regular-singular connections and residual factors of quantum $F$-bundles. For an arbitrary ordered monodromy spectrum, we classify the fully framed local groupoid: each residue fibre is a discrete affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$, with a unique normal form and trivial stabilisers. We then analyse elementary changes of lattice. A strictly positive integral residue difference obstructs the oriented wall; otherwise, in arbitrary rank, the extending normal-form arcs form an affine torsor of relative dimension $r(r-1)$, and specialisation to the shifted residue slice is polynomial and triangular by root height. Adjacent walls exhibit the composite-root correction dictated by the type-$A$ root-subgroup relations, while an example over the dual numbers detects a nilpotent saturation defect. For one-branch $F$-bundles, the scalar branch is recovered from the residual trace, and scalar residualisation yields a symmetric monoidal equivalence with zero-branch $F$-bundles. This construction yields residual atoms, functorial Jordan strata, and a residual chemical formula compatible with blow-ups and projective bundles. In the $A$-model, residualisation removes the unit direction; the rationally marked large-radius residual germ recovers the divisor cubic and distinguishes the marked residual germs of the Pfaffian and Grassmannian Calabi--Yau threefolds.

papers.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
papers.abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of the generalized cactus group associated with a finite standard parabolic subgroup of the underlying Coxeter group. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types B, D, E, F, and H, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine the associated generalized cactus group directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When the Coxeter diagram has finitely many vertices, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups. In type A, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group on $n$ strands if and only if it embeds into a Sylow 2-subgroup of the symmetric group on $n$ letters. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types A and B and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.

papers.title: The law of large numbers for non-additive capacities without continuity
papers.abstract: We consider a capacity on a general measurable space associated with a sequence of identically distributed random variables. With a weak assumption concerned with the independence and very few restrictions on the capacity, we show that, on a set with full lower-capacity, any cluster point of empirical averages lies in the mean interval with the lower and upper Choquet integrals of the random variables being its bounds, and, under a Fubini-independent product capacity introduced by Ghirardato (1997), cluster points fill the whole mean interval with full upper-capacity. The results give answers to two open questions of Terán (2014).

papers.title: Maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems
papers.abstract: We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. To obtain the upper bounds, we use the cubical flat torus theorem of Wise and Woodhouse. We then verify the sharpness of these upper bounds by constructing free abelian subgroups of the corresponding ranks. Our result shows that the maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of ordinary cactus groups can be larger than conjectured by Genevois. As an application, we show that these groups are not quasi-isometric to any right-angled Artin group unless they are virtually free abelian.

papers.title: Multi-time-stepping splitting scheme with mass lumping for the multiscale wave equation
papers.abstract: Efficient simulation of wave propagation in high-contrast media is challenging because standard explicit schemes are subject to severe time-step restrictions induced by fine spatial scales and fast multiscale modes, whereas fully implicit schemes require costly globally coupled solves. In this work, we develop a mass-lumped multi-time-stepping partially explicit splitting method for multiscale wave equations. Based on a nonlocal multicontinuum (NLMC) decomposition of the approximation space, the solution is separated into contrast-dependent fast components and contrast-independent slow components, which are advanced implicitly and explicitly, respectively. A mass-lumping approximation diagonalizes the coarse-scale mass operator and removes the coupling between two subproblems, thus enabling multirate time integration for the two parts. To further improve efficiency, we introduce a residual-based adaptive strategy that dynamically adjusts the time step of the explicitly treated subsystem according to its temporal error indicator. The proposed scheme is shown to be energy stable under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed mass-lumped multi-time-stepping scheme substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy comparable to that of standard fully implicit methods.

papers.title: Pólya's conjecture for Dirichlet eigenvalues of spherical shells and Aharonov--Bohm annuli
papers.abstract: We establish strict Dirichlet Pólya inequalities for spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$ and for every radius ratio. The inclusive eigenvalue counting function lies strictly below the leading Weyl term at every positive energy; consequently, each eigenvalue strictly exceeds its Weyl prediction, with multiplicities included. We also prove the same strict inequality for the Aharonov--Bohm operator on planar annuli at arbitrary flux. In dimension two, the nonmagnetic result gives a fully analytic proof of the planar annulus theorem of Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sher (J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2026). The common ingredient is a lattice-point bound for the shell action, uniform in the starting point of a tail and in the lattice translation. Quadrature for the inverse action controls the change of convexity caused by the inner boundary. The tail estimate supplies the hypothesis of the known dimension-reduction argument for balls, while lattice translations represent the magnetic flux. Laptev's product argument yields corresponding strict bounds on products of shells and nonempty bounded open sets.

papers.title: On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). Let $U_{n,r}$ denote the rank-$r$ uniform matroid on $n$ elements, where $0<r<n$, and let $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ denote the matroid obtained by replacing each element of $U_{n,r}$ with $q$ parallel copies. They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. In this paper, we prove that every $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ with $q\geq3$ satisfies the inequality. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. For matroids, we further prove that every element of a minimum-size loopless and coloopless counterexample lies in exactly one series or parallel class of size two.

papers.title: A Duality of the F Distribution
papers.abstract: The F distribution arises naturally in linear regression or analysis of variance. Elementary textbooks state the result in terms of the standard normal random vector and fixed projection matrices. More advanced textbooks and research articles have extended the result to spherically symmetric random vectors. We complement the literature with a dual result that the F distribution arises with a fixed vector and random projection matrices generated by a left-spherical random matrix.

papers.title: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on surfaces of nonpositive curvature
papers.abstract: We give a full proof that the geodesic flow of a closed surface of genus at least two with a \(C^{3+\mathrm{Lip}}\) metric of nonpositive curvature is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. In a forthcoming paper, we will present the corresponding result for smooth rank-one manifolds in every dimension.

papers.title: Local Maxima of Discrete Gaussian Processes: Exact Distributions and Infill Limits
papers.abstract: We study local maxima of centered, unit-variance Gaussian processes observed on one-dimensional grids. For general nonstationary covariance, we give exact sitewise peak probabilities, conditional height densities, and expected peak counts using the covariance of a site and its two neighbors. The height limits established here are unified by a continuous family indexed by the magnitude of the conditional height-curvature correlation parameter $η\in[0,1]$, with a Gaussian endpoint at $η=0$, and smooth peak laws for $0<η\le 1$ with a Rayleigh endpoint at $η=1$. Under continuous covariance derivatives through total order four, we prove convergence to the smooth family and obtain corresponding intensity and expected count limits. Additional sample path and Kac--Rice regularity assumptions identify these limits with the intensity and Palm height law of continuous local maxima. For general nonstationary covariance, a necessary and sufficient increment criterion characterizes convergence to the Gaussian endpoint, including when peak probabilities vanish. Explicit finite-grid bounds control density and tail errors and yield uniform approximations across sites. For each fixed nonconstant, mean-square continuous stationary process, the fourth spectral moment gives a complete classification: finiteness yields a smooth family member, whereas an infinite moment yields the Gaussian endpoint and divergent expected peak counts on every interval of positive length. The height laws converge in total variation in both regimes. Nonstationary examples, Matérn covariance models, and numerical comparisons illustrate the results, including logarithmic boundary behavior and the distinction between distributional convergence and relative tail accuracy.

papers.title: Gauge theory on Cohomogeneity One Spin(7)-Manifolds from Aloff--Wallach Spaces
papers.abstract: We begin a systematic study of $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons on complete non-compact cohomogeneity one $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-manifolds with Aloff--Wallach spaces $N_{k,l}=\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{U}(1)_{k,l}$ as principal orbits. We provide a complete classification of admissible principal $\mathrm{U}(1)$- and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-bundles and smooth bounded solutions to the $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instanton equation on them. We study bubbling phenomena for the constructed $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons and discuss the compactification of the moduli space of $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons in both the ALC and AC settings.

papers.title: Multiplicity of closed geodesics on odd-dimensional bumpy Finsler compact space form
papers.abstract: Let $M = S^{2n+1}/Γ$ be a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact space form, endowed with a bumpy Finsler metric $F$. In this paper, we prove that there exist at least $n+3$ contractible minimal closed geodesics on $M$, assuming that all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices. Here, a contractible closed geodesic is called minimal if it is not an iteration of any other contractible closed geodesic. In particular, this confirms the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture for the bumpy quotient manifold $(S^3/Γ, F)$ under the non-zero Morse index assumption.

papers.title: Adaptive Normalized Gradient Method for $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth Problems: Estimating Problem Parameters as a Region
papers.abstract: We propose a parameter-free and efficient gradient descent algorithm for $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization. This notion of smoothness, introduced by Zhang et al. (2020), allows the smoothness bound to grow with the gradient norm. Similar to cutting-plane localization, our method uses a sequence of observations to maintain a region of plausible values for $(L_0,L_1)$ and uses this region to select step sizes. In the convex setting, our method attains the standard iteration complexity bound $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\left(L_0/ε+ L_1^2\right)\|x^0-x^*\|^2\right)$ for finding an $ε$-optimal solution, while in the nonconvex setting it finds an $ε$-stationary point within $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\left(L_0/ε^2 + L_1/ε\right)(f(x^0)-f^*)\right)$ iterations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to establish, for a single parameter-free algorithm, the best-known iteration-complexity guarantee in the nonconvex setting while also providing the above iteration-complexity guarantee in the convex setting. Experiments on logistic regression and real phase retrieval demonstrate that our method can exploit $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness and perform efficiently on nonconvex problems.

papers.title: Minorization and exponential ergodicity for degenerate diffusions with countable switching
papers.abstract: We establish a local-minorization criterion for diffusions with countably many state-dependent switching regimes, even when every frozen transition law is singular. One regular controlled path yields a common absolutely continuous component for nearby initial states, with rate positivity required only at the switching locations. The proof controls a family of Brownian perturbations and its derivatives while retaining a path restriction for the switching likelihood. Controlled entrance and a joint Lyapunov inequality then give weighted exponential ergodicity. A concrete coefficient and rank criterion and degenerate network examples illustrate the result.

papers.title: Cramer-Rao Type Bounds for Generalized Exponential Families
papers.abstract: It is well known that the sufficient statistics of an exponential family attain the usual Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) for their expected value. In this paper, we extend this result to a broader family of distributions that includes exponential families and power-law families, with Student t-distributions as special case. To derive the generalized Cramer-Rao inequality, we first apply Eguchi's theory to Bregman divergence to obtain a Riemannian metric and then follow the approach of Amari and Nagaoka. Since this approach applies only to models with finite support, we use Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to extend it to models with countably infinite or continuous support. The resulting generalized CRLB provides a finite-sample lower bound related to the asymptotic covariance matrix of the Minimum Bregman Divergence Estimator (MBDE). We show that the sufficient statistic of the generalized family attains the generalized CRLB. Moreover, although the generalized CRLB does not, in general, coincide with the asymptotic covariance matrix of the MBDE, the covariance matrix of an estimator attaining the generalized CRLB coincides with the corresponding matrix for the joint distribution of the sample.

papers.title: Nef complexity of klt Fano varieties: the full spectrum and classification below two
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a complex klt Fano variety. We study the rational total index $τ_X$ and the nef complexity $c_X=\dim X+ρ(X)-τ_X$. Previous joint work of the author with Enwright, Filipazzi, Gongyo, Moraga, Svaldi, and Wang established the corresponding nonnegativity and zero-case characterization in the broader framework of a special class of generalized log Calabi--Yau pairs. Here we give a direct proof in the Fano setting, prove that there is no value strictly between zero and one, and classify all klt Fano varieties with $c_X<2$, without assuming $\mathbb Q$-factoriality. At complexity one, after splitting off projective-space factors, the remaining factor is a normal quadric of Picard number one, a linear blow-up of projective space, or an integral $(1,1)$ hypersurface in a product of projective spaces. If $1<c_X<2$, only two weighted-projective families occur; in particular, no smooth Fano variety has nef complexity strictly between one and two. We also determine the spectrum when the dimension is allowed to vary: \[ \{0\}\cup\left\{2-\frac2q \ \middle| \ q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq2}\right\} \cup(\mathbb Q\cap[2,\infty)). \] Most proofs in this paper were developed from arguments generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT through discussions initiated and guided by the author; see the statement on the use of generative AI.

papers.title: Improved rapid phase ordering for Ising dynamics on random regular graphs
papers.abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs with $n$ vertices at low temperature, in the regime $β\geq C/d$ where $C,d$ are sufficiently large constants. In this regime, the full mixing time is exponential in $n$, because of the bottleneck between the two dominant phases: configurations with a majority of plus spins and configurations with a majority of minus spins. We show that, for sufficiently large $d$, if the dynamics is initialized with an excess of at least $ε_{C,d} n$ plus spins over minus spins, then it quasi-equilibrates in time $O(\log n)$ to the Gibbs measure conditioned on positive magnetization. In addition, the required bias $ε_{C,d}$ can be chosen so that $ε_{C,d}\to 0$ as $d,C\to\infty$. Previous bound of \cite{GSS25+} in the Ising and large-$d$ setting required $β\gtrsim (\log d)/d$. A key difficulty is that, even from the all-plus initialization, one must control the propagation of negative information in spacetime in a low-temperature model with strong local correlations. We address this by developing a new bootstrap approach to proving subcriticality of disagreement clusters under the grand coupling.

papers.title: A new class of smooth algebraic varieties with the density property and a counterexample to the Tóth-Varolin Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the smooth affine hypersurfaces \[ X_{m,n}=\{ζ^mz_0^n+ (1+z_1ζ)z_2+ζz_3^2=1\}\subset\mathbb{C}^5,\;\; m,n\geq 2, \] have the density property. For every odd integer $d\geq 3$, we identify $X_{d-1,d}$ with a Kaliman modification along a Brieskorn variety of type $(d,2,2,2)$. We prove that the fourfolds $X_{d-1,d}$ are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$ but not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$. These, therefore, give counterexamples to the Tóth-Varolin conjecture.

papers.title: Global Mizohata-Takeuchi for Indicator Weights of Bounded Complexity in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: We prove the global Mizohata-Takeuchi estimate for bounded complexity weights in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and an arbitrary $C^2$ uniformly convex curve on the Fourier side, with an implied constant depending only on the complexity and the curve. A version with a logarithmic loss follows from a short argument using the $T^*T$ method and the main estimate of Basu, Guo, Zhang, and Zorin-Kranich (2026). The main effort of this paper is devoted to removing the logarithmic factor. To achieve this, we use tools from semialgebraic geometry and adapt and develop ideas of Ricci and Stein (1987). As a by-product, we obtain a uniform geometric inequality for planar regions of bounded complexity that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Global exact controllability for Schrödinger equations with Lipschitz and logarithmic nonlinearities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study global exact controllability of semilinear Schrödinger equations by localized internal additive controls. For every globally Lipschitz nonlinearity in arbitrary dimensions, we prove that any two $L^2$ states can be connected in any prescribed positive time, without smallness assumptions on the states or the Lipschitz constant. The result holds on smooth bounded Euclidean domains under a local convex-phase condition, and on an interval with any nonempty open control region. It also extends to compact Riemannian manifolds under the corresponding phase condition. In one dimension, we further establish controllability for logarithmic nonlinearities of the form \[ f(z)=zφ(|z|)+\mathfrak g(z), \] where $φ$ is real-valued, $\mathfrak g$ is globally Lipschitz, and $r|φ'(r)|\leq D(1+|\log r|)^γ$ with $0\leqγ<1/2$. For the endpoint case $γ=1/2$, we achieve the result by assuming the leading coefficient is sufficiently small. These results resolve the global Lipschitz controllability question raised by Zuazua \cite[Section~3]{Zuazua2003} in the stated geometric settings and establish its logarithmic extension within the specified one-dimensional classes.

papers.title: Vanishing transport noise enhances stability of stratified Couette flow in the 3D Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the enhanced nonlinear stability of stably stratified Couette flow in the three-dimensional Boussinesq system driven by a common affine Stratonovich transport noise. Our main result shows that, for fixed $β>1/2$, suitably chosen noise amplitudes enlarge the range of perturbations for which we prove stability, even as they vanish with viscosity. For each fixed deterministic Sobolev perturbation satisfying the sufficient smallness conditions, the strong solution is global and obeys stability estimates on an event of prescribed high probability. No spatial localization or vanishing initial double means are required. The proof combines noise-induced mixing with coupled energy estimates to control nonlinear feedback and preserve the physical damping of the fast vertical velocity and temperature.

papers.title: U torsion structure in Heegaard Floer homology
papers.abstract: We construct infinite families of Brieskorn spheres with three singular fibers for which the difference between the largest and the second largest length of $U$-torsion in their Heegaard Floer homology $HF^-$ increases to infinity as the family parameter increases. In particular, these families give a negative answer to the strong geography restriction problem by Alfieri and Binns \cite[Question 1.10]{AB24} which was added to the recent K3 list \cite[Problem 3.55, Remark(5)]{K3}. As a consequence of the results by Alfieri and Binns, these families give the examples of integer homology spheres that are neither surgery on a knot nor large surgery on links.

papers.title: The first-order part of the Ordered Variable Word theorem
papers.abstract: An ordered $ω$-variable sequence over a finite alphabet~$A$ is an infinite sequence over the extended alphabet $A \sqcup \{ x_0, x_1, \dots \}$, where each variable kind appears at least once, and the last occurrence of $x_i$ appears before the first occurrence of $x_{i+1}$. The Ordered Variable Word theorem states that for every finite coloring of the words over a finite alphabet~$A$, there is an ordered $ω$-variable sequence~$W$ over~$A$ such that every word induced by substituting variables with letters, and cutting before the first undefined variable, has the same color. In this article, we prove that the Ordered Variable Word theorem is $Π^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}Σ^0_2$. It follows that the tree theorem for singletons by Chubb, Hirst, and McNicholl is $Π^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}Σ^0_2$, answering a long-standing open question. Lemma 3.13 was found by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic).

papers.title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
papers.abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

papers.title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
papers.abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $π$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|α|^2/(1+|α|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.

papers.title: Almost Periodic Characters and Hamel Coefficients in TVG Topologies on the Real Line
papers.abstract: We study topological vector group topologies on the real line generated by Hamel coefficient functions and circle-valued characters. We determine their continuous characters, completions, and isomorphisms, and construct a sequence separating modular convergence from convergence of real-valued observations. We also classify precompact topologies and prove that no greatest nondiscrete topology exists. For the separate problem of a greatest compatible locally quasi-convex topology, we establish transfer and dilation criteria and rule out a family of dyadic counterexample constructions. The existence of a greatest compatible topology remains unresolved.

papers.title: Minimum-Time Escape from the Conic Field of View of a Reeds-Shepp Pursuer: Classification and Game Value for a Slower or Equally Fast Evader
papers.abstract: We study minimum-time escape of an omnidirectional evader from the forward conic field of view of a Reeds-Shepp pursuer with minimum turning radius $r$. For speed ratio $ν$ and cone half-angle $0<α<π/2$, we prove a global escape/holding classification: straight reversal holds the whole cone for $ν\le\sinα$, escape is confined to a barrier-bounded dart for $\sinα<ν\le1$, and escape is possible from every state for $ν>1$. For the slower or equally fast evader, $\sinα<ν\le1$, we construct the solution with Isaacs' characteristics and verify it in feedback form, using a Filippov pursuer relay and a one-sided evader branch. The finite escape time is the first root of one scalar equation, and the holding region is bounded by the nonusable parts of the rays and a barrier that closes with a convex corner on the front axis. Sample-and-hold counter-controls show that this escape time is the value of the game in nonanticipative strategies at every state except the corner. There the two strategy values differ: the pursuer's is infinite, whereas an evader that chooses which barrier branch to cross from the initial germ of the pursuer's control escapes before the barrier time $τ_I$, which is the evader's exact strategy value. An independent level-set solver, refined on fixed comparison points, agrees with the closed-form escape time and reproduces the holding region at the tested parameters.

papers.title: Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veroneseans
papers.abstract: The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. We also show that many Terracini loci involve only sets with "intratangent pairs" that lie on the same tangent space to the underlying Veronese variety. Finally, we give some applications to algebraic statistics, showing that osculating varieties of Veronese varieties are moment varieties for local mixtures of location families and connecting Terracini loci to local identifiability.

papers.title: Approximating the Ellipse Perimeter by "Bending the Line": The ELIP Closed-Form Family
papers.abstract: The perimeter of an ellipse is expressed exactly through the complete elliptic integral of the second kind, motivating accurate closed-form approximations. We introduce ELIP (Ellipse Linear Interpolated Perimeter), a family built by correcting the straight line joining the two exact normalized endpoint values. Two branches are developed: logarithmic-power corrections with optional deformation and exponential modulators, and rational-logarithmic corrections incorporating the exact asymptotic behavior of highly elongated ellipses. The framework distinguishes coefficients fixed analytically by Maclaurin matching from parameters optimized numerically by minimax fitting. Compact rationalized formulas achieve maximum relative errors of approximately 6.84, 3.57, 0.904, and 1.596 ppm. An ELIP R5,2 + 3 log formula with three fitted degrees of freedom has a certified maximum relative error below 0.001623 ppm. For ELIP R5,3 + 3 log, all rational-core coefficients are determined by exact Maclaurin matching. A one-parameter multiplicative correction, 1 - A*h^12*(1-h)^(7/4), reduces the certified global error bound to below 0.000452 ppm. This formula matches the exact perimeter series through h^8, while the correction starts at order h^12. The results provide a systematic approach combining exact endpoint geometry, local series constraints, elongated-limit logarithmic asymptotics, and low-dimensional numerical optimization.

papers.title: Data-Driven Minimum Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems with Finite Sample Guarantees
papers.abstract: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be \emph{small}, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices and show that there exists a fundamental lower bound on the optimal control energy which cannot be overcome by increasing the time horizon of the problem. We then extend the formulation to systems with unknown dynamics using maximum-likelihood estimation and conformal calibration, and compare these approaches with direct sample-based estimation that do not incorporate structural information of SMEC problem into account. Further, with the help of bias-variance analysis, we show when incorporating structural information proves to be better than direct sample based approach. Finally, we establish finite-sample high-probability upper bounds on optimal-cost sub-optimality and original constraint-violation probability under the data-driven controller, quantifying their dependence on the number of experiments, number of samples per experiment, system dimension, input sequence dimension, and noise-to-signal ratio. Using simulations, we validate the theoretical results numerically.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Eventual Stability Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to the eventual stability conjecture over number fields and classify for power maps.

papers.title: Small values of the Riemann zeta-function near the critical line
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we study negative moments and small values of the Riemann zeta-function to the right of the critical line. For every fixed $0<k<1/2$, we establish the conjecturally sharp bound $$ \frac1T\int_T^{2T} \Big|ζ(\tfrac12+α+it)\Big|^{-2k}\,dt \ll α^{-k^2}, $$ for $α=o(1)$ and $α\gg 1/\log T$. We also obtain almost sharp upper bounds slightly to the left of $1/\log T$. This improves the upper bounds of the first two authors for shifts as small as $1/\log T$, confirming a conjecture of Gonek in this range. A separate bound for the moment at $k=1/2$ yields an improved bound for cancellation in the Möbius function. Namely, we show that $$ \sum_{n\leq x}μ(n) \ll \sqrt{x}\exp \bigg(C\sqrt{\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}}\bigg) $$ for some $C>0$, improving on previous results of Soundararajan, Balazard and de Roton, and of the first two authors. For $t$ chosen uniformly from $[T,2T]$, we also prove that \[ \min_{|h|\leq1} \Big|ζ\Big(\tfrac12+α+i(t+h)\Big)\Big| =α^{1+o(1)} \] in probability, provided that $α\ll (\log T)^{-c}$ for some fixed $c >0$, and $α\log T/\log\log T\to\infty$. This agrees with the leading order predicted by a minimum analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating Conjecture. Further results include bounds for minima on intervals of logarithmically growing length, for negative moments in almost all short intervals, and an extension of the range of sharp negative-moment bounds for $k>1/2$. A main ingredient in the proof of some of these results is a Gaussian large-deviation upper bound for $\log|ζ(1/2+α+it)|^{-1}$, obtained by building on work of Arguin, Bailey, and Roberts.

papers.title: Fate of Discrete Time Crystals in Finite-Size Cavity QED Systems
papers.abstract: It has been shown that Discrete Time Crystal (DTC) behavior may arise in the periodically driven, open Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit ($N \rightarrow \infty$). In this work, we demonstrate that finite $N$ non-mean-field fluctuations in this model can lead to decay rates and amplitudes of transient DTCs that display a non-trivial non-monotonic behavior with an increasing number of atoms. We show that the second-order cumulant expansion fails to capture the finite-size dynamics, while a stochastic version of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) is remarkably accurate, particularly in the large atom ensemble limit. Using the TWA and the Monte Carlo Wave Function (MCWF) approach, we identify three distinct dynamical regimes of transient DTC behavior in the finite-size Dicke model. We outline the mechanism behind the non-monotonic finite size dynamical decay of DTC order and discuss the implications for experiments performed on finite-sized atomic assemblies.

papers.title: A Unified Theory of Solvability for Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Control Problems I: The Homogeneous Case
papers.abstract: The existing theory of stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems focuses on open-loop and closed-loop solvability. For finite horizon problems, it is widely accepted that those two types of solvability are not equivalent in general, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples. In contrast, they coincide in standard infinite-horizon formulations with constant coefficients under suitable stabilizability and integrability assumptions. This paper aims at challenging this well-established paradigm by developing a novel framework of closed-loop solvability, namely generalized closed-loop solvability, which removes the $L^2$-integrability constraint on the feedback strategies from the existing formulation. It will be proven that open-loop and generalized closed-loop solvability are equivalent and the classical closed-loop solvablity is a particular case only when the admissible feedback strategy is $L^2$-integrable over the time horizon. In other words, the previously established non-equivalence between open-loop and closed-loop solvability stems solely from the limitations of the classical formulation which requires the $L^2$-integrability of the admissible feedback strategies over the time-horizon. Therefore, this paper unifies the theory of the solvabilitiy for stochastic LQ control problems. Moreover, our results offer a novel insight to stochastic LQ control problems: open-loop/generalized closed-loop solvability is essentially equivalent to piecewisely local closed-loop solvability in the classical sense. The current paper is focused on homogeneous cases only and non-homogeneous cases will be studied in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: Secondary Chow Invariants beyond Lawson--Massey Products
papers.abstract: We construct secondary Chow invariants that cannot be recovered from Lawson--Massey realization. For every smooth complex projective curve $C$ of positive genus and every $n\ge2$, explicit cubical defining systems yield $n$ distinct Massey values in $\rm{CH}^{3}(C\times P^{2},1)$, with zero full indeterminacy, forming a cyclic group of order $n$. All corresponding triples have identical morphic classes and zero morphic, Lawson, and singular Massey brackets, despite nonzero target groups. The values are detected by the Weil pairing. We further construct secondary quotient classes of every finite order on smooth projective varieties with ample canonical bundle in every dimension at least two, and prove that generically finite pullbacks of coprime degree preserve their exact orders. These constructions obstruct integral and prime-local motivic formality, although the corresponding brackets become $\{0\}$ after reduction modulo every integer $m\ge2$. All specified values are torsion and vanish after rationalization.

papers.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.

papers.title: A proof of Vince's conjecture on the average order of connected induced subgraphs
papers.abstract: We prove that the average order of connected induced subgraphs of a connected simple graph of order $n$ and minimum degree at least $3$ is strictly greater than $n/2$, which settles a conjecture of Vince~[\emph{J. Graph Theory} 97 (2021), 82--103]. We go further and show that, for connected simple graphs of order $n$ and minimum degree exactly $k\ge3$, $K_k\vee(K_1\cup K_{n-k-1})$ uniquely minimizes this average under additional conditions.

papers.title: Optimal Two-Mode Switching with Setup Costs for a Controlled Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Process
papers.abstract: We study an infinite-horizon discounted optimal switching problem for an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process whose mean-reversion level can be switched between two values. Switching incurs positive, potentially asymmetric fixed costs, and the mode with the higher mean-reversion level entails an additional running cost. The revenue rate is proportional to the positive part of the state. We characterize the value function and identify parameter conditions under which an optimal policy either remains permanently in one mode after a possible costly initial switch or follows a threshold rule. The threshold formulation allows infinite boundaries and therefore includes one-way switching. A key technical contribution is to establish existence and uniqueness of the relevant solutions to the coupled nonlinear free-boundary equations arising from value-matching and smooth-fit conditions. In the corresponding parameter regimes, these solutions determine the finite switching thresholds and the coefficients of the candidate value functions. A verification argument then establishes the optimality of the resulting policies over all admissible switching strategies.

papers.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.

papers.title: $\mathrm{v}$-numbers of powers of edge ideals of cubic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.

papers.title: Trace Inverse Estimates and Kernel-based Nitsche Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Interface Problems
papers.abstract: We establish trace inverse estimates for products of independently generated Sobolev-kernel trial spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche Galerkin methods for elliptic interface problems. The estimates control one-sided gradient traces by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form provides the flux control required by the Nitsche formulation without imposing value constraints on the trial spaces, including configurations with an interior inclusion. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain coercivity and well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{s-1}$ and $h^s$ for piecewise $H^s$ solutions, $2\le s\le m$, where $h$ is the maximum fill distance and $m$ is the kernel Sobolev order. The $L^2$ bound additionally requires piecewise $H^2$ regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For scaled kernels $Φ_{m,\varepsilon}$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, we also derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and support scaling, whereas a three-dimensional mixed-boundary calculation illustrates the method.

papers.title: Linear $2$-Group Actions With Exactly One Regular Orbit
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-group and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then the characteristic $q$ of $V$ is a Fermat prime, $V$ is irreducible over ${\Bbb F}_q$, ${\rm dim}_{{\Bbb F}_q}V$ is a power of $2$, and the centraliser of $G$ in ${\rm GL}(V)$ embeds into $G$. For every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ we determine the largest orbit size $2^{x_m}$ of a Sylow $2$-subgroup $P_m$ of ${\rm GL}_{2^{m-1}}(q)$ on its natural module $V_m$, and the number of orbits of this size, which is $1$, $2$, or $3$. Our main result is that for every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ there is an irreducible subgroup of $P_m$ of order $2^{x_m}$ that has exactly one regular orbit on $V_m$. In this respect $p=2$ behaves like $p=3$, and unlike the Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ studied in an earlier paper. The proof places a group related to a Singer cycle into every block of $q-1$ coordinates. This reduces the problem, for all Fermat primes at once, to a question about subgroups of a Sylow $2$-subgroup of a symmetric group acting on subsets, which we answer by means of fibre products. We also determine which largest orbits occur in two small levels, and we classify the examples in some small cases with the help of a computer.

papers.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
papers.abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

papers.title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
papers.abstract: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. On data from the independent Perceval simulator at the scale of prior work (n=4 photons in m=20 and m=10 modes), the posterior has lower KL divergence than both recycling and postselection at every tested loss rate in the no-collision benchmark. In the collision regime it recovers the loss rate and the collision-pattern probabilities, which recycling cannot estimate, and stays below recycling at every loss rate and below postselection except at low loss, where the two are comparable. Its advantage over recycling grows with the sample count, and it supplies credible intervals that the baselines lack.

papers.title: Frozen colorings and recolorability of blowups
papers.abstract: The $k$-reconfiguration graph $R_k(G)$ of the proper $k$-colorings of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-colorings of $G$, with an edge between two colorings if they differ on exactly one vertex. A graph $G$ is recolorable if $R_k(G)$ is connected for all $k \ge χ(G) + 1$. In this paper, we study recolorability under blowups through frozen colorings, here blowup means replacing vertices with non-empty cliques. We characterize frozen colorings of a blowup of $G$ in terms of maximal independent sets of the base graph, and develop a lifting principle that transfers suitable frozen obstructions from an induced subgraph to a blowup of the ambient graph. This framework yields several consequences. In particular, we answer negatively a question of Belavadi, Cameron and Sintiari on recoloring via modular decomposition, and disprove their conjecture on blowups of prime graphs. We further determine exactly which cycles have all blowups recolorable: this holds for $C_n$ if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,7\}$. The frozen obstructions arising from the negative cases, together with the lifting principle, imply that if every blowup of a graph $G$ is recolorable, then every induced hole of $G$ has length $4$, $5$, or $7$. Finally, using linear programming duality, we show that every such graph $G$ is fractionally co-strongly perfect.

papers.title: Quicksilver Asymptotics and Pole Arrays for $q$-Painlevé II
papers.abstract: We construct local families of solutions of the $q$-difference second Painlevé equation that vanish at infinity with a common algebraic expansion, parameterised by the amplitude of an exponentially small correction. Considering an appropriate boundary region, a formal expansion that retains two independently excited exponential perturbations is developed, and subsequent transseries summation predicts the location of simple poles. Adopting a $q$-theta function realisation of the exponential factors, we prove an asymptotic pole-location formula for a one-parameter family of true solutions. These poles approach the aforementioned boundaries where exponential behaviour fundamentally changes, providing an analogue of pole arrays near anti-Stokes directions in classical Painlevé asymptotics.

papers.title: An orthogonality inequality in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ and the double-cap conjecture
papers.abstract: The orthogonal neighborhood of a set in real projective space is the union of the hyperplanes perpendicular to its points. We prove that caps minimize neighborhood measure among measurable sets of fixed measure in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$, for $n \geq 3$, with rigidity up to null sets. This yields the double-cap conjecture: a measurable subset of $S^{n-1}$ containing no orthogonal pair has measure at most that of two opposite open caps of radius $π/4$. The argument combines compactness of the Funk transform, rotation comparisons, and projective variations. We also obtain qualitative stability and determine the measurable fractional chromatic number of the spherical orthogonality graph. AI played an assistive role in preparing this paper. The formalization and verification workflow for a separate Lean 4 proof of the main inequality and double-cap result, based on a different argument, were carried out almost entirely using AI-assisted tools.

papers.title: A boundary approach to rigidity of $q$-Araki--Woods factors
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study structural and rigidity properties of $q$-Araki--Woods factors arising from strongly continuous orthogonal representations of $\R$. We first introduce an AO-type boundary property that is formulated in terms of length projections on the $q$-Fock spaces, and prove that all $q$-Araki--Woods factors satisfy this condition. We next characterize uniform convergence of the associated malleable deformations. We then use these two ingredients as a substitute for weak containment in the coarse bimodule and deduce several rigidity theorems in the framework of Popa's deformation/rigidity theory. As a main consequence, we prove that every $q$-Araki--Woods factor is stably strongly solid. We also prove a normalizer rigidity theorem for inclusions arising from direct sum representations. Finally, we compute Connes' $τ$-invariant, and construct a continuum of pairwise non-isomorphic type $\mathrm{III}_1$ $q$-Araki--Woods factors with the same $τ$-invariant.

papers.title: Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models
papers.abstract: We establish a strong Hodge decomposition theorem for Novikov type Landau--Ginzburg models, that is, triples $(M,g,θ)$ consisting of a non-compact complete Kähler manifold $(M,g)$ and a non-trivial closed holomorphic one-form $θ$ on $M$.Under the well-tameness condition and under the assumption that $M$ is Stein, we prove that the space of $L^{2}$-forms on $M$ admits an orthogonal decomposition into the space of harmonic forms of the twisted Laplacian $Δ_θ$ and the images of the twisted Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial+θ\wedge$ and $\bar\partial^{\dagger}+ι_{\barθ^{\sharp}}$; moreover, the harmonic space is concentrated in degree $n=\dim_{\C}M$ and is isomorphic to the Milnor rings of $θ$. As applications, we endow the complement of a hyperplane arrangement with a complete cylindrical Kähler metric, and we show that the differential of a master function with nonresonant weights is well-tamed with respect to this metric. After passing to a log resolution in the non-normal-crossing case; we then apply the results to the Yang--Yang functional of the Gaudin model, whose critical points are the Bethe roots: the top-degree harmonic space is described by the corresponding Milnor rings, and the number of Bethe roots is given by the Varchenko--Orlik--Terao lattice formula.

papers.title: The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $χ_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ χ_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $Γ$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.

papers.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
papers.abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. One generator is an elementary planar rotation, \[ A=R_{12}, \] while the other combines a linearly modulated planar rotation with a chain of adjacent planar rotations: \[ B=x_3R_{12}+\sum_{k=2}^n R_{k,k+1}. \] Thus two one-parameter groups suffice, and two is the smallest possible number. The proof separates naturally into two steps. We first show that the $n$ adjacent rotations \[ R_{12},R_{23},\ldots,R_{n,n+1} \] together with the shear $x_3R_{12}$ generate, through their flows, a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. The infinitesimal argument is organized by transverse vector spherical harmonics. For $n\ge4$ the relevant harmonic spaces are irreducible $SO(n+1)$-modules; on $S^2$ the argument reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; and on $S^3$ the transverse harmonic spaces split into two curl eigenspaces. We then show that all $n+1$ of these vector fields lie in the Lie algebra generated by $A$ and $B$. A Casimir operator separates the quadratic shear from the linear rotational terms, after which the remaining rotations can be recovered successively. Finally, standard approximation formulas for flows convert the Lie-algebraic generation result into $C^\infty$ density in $\SDiff_0(S^n)$.

papers.title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on Two Feistel-Type Constructions
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, the security of traditional cryptographic systems is facing significant challenges. As a fundamental component of symmetric cryptography, block ciphers have attracted increasing attention regarding their quantum security in recent years. In this paper, we propose new quantum attacks on two Feistel-type constructions, i.e., New Structure IV and the lightweight block cipher LBlock, under the quantum chosen-plaintext attack (qCPA) model. First, we construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and perform an $r(r>12)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. Compared with Li et al.'s qCPA-based result presented at INSCRYPT 2024, our attack reduces the time complexity by a factor of $2^{n/2}$, where $n$ denotes the subkey length. Second, we design a 9-round quantum distinguisher for LBlock and extend it to an $r(r>15)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. The proposed quantum distinguisher covers one more round than Liu et al.'s automated-search distinguisher at ASIACRYPT 2025, which results in a $2^{16}$ reduction in the time complexity of our $r$-round quantum key-recovery attack on LBlock. Furthermore, by analyzing the structure of the round function and the key scheduling of LBlock, we reduce the subkey guess space for the 15-round attack from 76 bits to 52 bits, lowering the time complexity from \(O(2^{38})\) to \(O(2^{26})\) by a factor of \(2^{12}\).

papers.title: On the Accuracy of Approximate Leave-One-Out with Blockwise Nonsmooth Regularization in High-dimensions
papers.abstract: Approximate leave-one-out (ALO) refers to methods that provide computationally efficient and statistically accurate approximations to leave-one-out risk estimation. These methods have recently attracted increased attention because of their connections to other important problems, including machine unlearning and data valuation. For empirical risk minimization, ALO methods often rely on a few Newton steps and therefore require smooth loss functions and regularizers. In high-dimensional problems, however, regularizers are frequently non-smooth. This has motivated the development of heuristic ALO methods for non-smooth regularization, whose empirical accuracy is often strong but whose theoretical justification remains limited. In this paper, we study the accuracy of a heuristic ALO method for a broad class of non-differentiable penalties that promote block sparsity in the proportional high-dimensional regime. Assuming uniformly bounded block sizes, we prove that the expected average absolute discrepancy between the exact leave-one-out loss and its ALO approximation is $O(\log^{3/2}(en)/\sqrt{n})$. Our proof technique differs substantially from existing approaches and relies on obtaining sharp bounds on the number of active groups whose status changes between the full-data and leave-one-out estimators. In addition to yielding stronger guarantees under weaker assumptions than prior work, our analysis provides new insight into the stability of sparse estimators under perturbations of the training data.

papers.title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
papers.abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-γQ^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, γ>0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schrödinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.

papers.title: Pointwise decay of steady Navier--Stokes flows with Navier-slip boundary condition in two-dimensional channels
papers.abstract: We establish a pointwise decay estimate for steady incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in two-dimensional channels with positive Navier friction coefficient. Specifically, for the arbitrary-flux solutions constructed by Sha, Wang, and Xie \cite{SWX22f}, under suitable outlet conditions and weighted geometric bounds on the channel walls, we show \[ |\Bu(x_1,x_2)|\le \frac{C}{f(x_1)}, \] where $f$ is the channel width. Our decay rate is optimal in the cross-sectional supremum norm when the prescribed flux is nonzero. The main difficulty is that rescaling by the local width changes the Navier friction coefficient into a potentially large parameter. The key technique is to establish a local Stokes boundary estimate uniform in this parameter.

papers.title: On Entries of Spectral Decompositions and Applications
papers.abstract: The entries of the spectral idempotents of a graph are its local and crossed local multiplicities. This paper uses these classical quantities in three applications. First, in a graph on $n$ vertices without isolated vertices, every local multiplicity is at most $\frac{n-1}{n}$, and every diagonal entry of the Cesaro average mixing matrix is at most $1-\frac{2}{n}+\frac{2}{n^2}$. In both bounds equality holds only for the complete graph. This proves the connected form of the complete graph trace conjecture of Godsil, Guo and Sobchuk together with its equality case, and component and degree refinements follow. The two upper bounds and their attainment by complete graphs also occur in a recent machine checked proof, without a formal characterization of when equality holds. Second, for the line graph of a connected graph $Γ$, the average return probability at a bridge with a bipartite component on one side is at least the reciprocal of the rank of the unsigned incidence matrix. Equality holds exactly for $P_2$ and $P_3$. The proof combines local moments with known inverse-incidence formulas. Finally, the paper gives a short proof of Godsil's entry criterion, which says that vertices $u$ and $v$ are strongly cospectral exactly when $\left|(E_θ)_{uv}\right|=(E_θ)_{uu}$ for every eigenvalue $θ$. The criterion recovers the known classification in connected noncomplete strongly regular graphs, where the strongly cospectral pairs are precisely the two-vertex parts of cocktail party graphs.

papers.title: On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation
papers.abstract: We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
papers.abstract: We establish Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary fractional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system with different orders of dissipation. Our first result shows that every smooth solution satisfying the natural homogeneous Sobolev energy conditions is trivial whenever $1\leqα\leq 5/3$ and $3\leqα+2β\leq5$, without any additional integrability assumptions on the velocity or magnetic fields. This extends previous results to new parameter regimes, including cases with $β<1$. Beyond this region, we prove a complementary Liouville theorem under suitable integrability conditions only on the radial components of the velocity and magnetic fields. The proofs rely on the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and localized energy estimates.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.

papers.title: Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories
papers.abstract: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.

papers.title: The Spectrum of the Discrete Mathieu Operator with Nonreal Coupling
papers.abstract: We study the discrete Mathieu operator with nonreal coupling in the large-period limit, using complex WKB methods for analytic finite-difference equations. We obtain quantization formulas in different regions of the complex energy plane. Away from the corners of the image of the classical symbol, these formulas involve cosines of classical action integrals with small analytic corrections to the actions. Near each corner, we derive a uniform quantization formula involving the reciprocal Gamma function. The quantization formulas constrain spectral accumulation to curves determined by the competing exponential terms. Numerical computations illustrate the resulting spectral geometry.

papers.title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
papers.abstract: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.

papers.title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
papers.abstract: The induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)$ is defined as the minimum order of a graph $F$ such that any 2-coloring of its edges with red and blue leads to either a red induced copy of $G$ or a blue induced copy of $H$. In 1998, Kohayakawa, Prömel, and Rödl conjectured that for any fixed graph $G$, there exists a constant $f=f(G)$ such that the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G, H)$ is bounded by $|V(H)|^f$ for every graph $H$. In this paper, we completely solve the Kohayakawa--Prömel--Rödl conjecture, which states that for any graphs $G$ and $H$ with $|V(G)|=k\ge2$ and $|V(H)|=t\ge2$, $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)\le t^{60k^2+3}$. This verifies the conjecture with $f(G)=60|V(G)|^2+3$.

papers.title: Hyperwellfoundedness and Eventual Domination
papers.abstract: We prove that a Borel strict partial order is an increasing union of wellfounded Borel partial orders if and only if it admits an (injective) Borel homomorphism to the eventual domination order.

papers.title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of Álvarez López and Calaza.

papers.title: Engineering \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two remote superconducting qubits via a multimode waveguide
papers.abstract: Waveguides provide a flexible platform for long-range interactions between superconducting qubits. Here, we study how to engineer the effective \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two qubits via qubit frequency assignments and multimode interference determined by the mode configuration and standing-wave parities of a finite multimode waveguide. For a single-mode waveguide, we find that \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions cannot be simultaneously suppressed to zero and the residual qubit-qubit coupling always exists. For example, the \(XY\) interaction may be suppressed to a negligible level when two qubits and the waveguide mode satisfy the two-photon resonant condition, but the \(ZZ\) interaction cannot be switched off. For multimode configurations within the central dispersive window, the engineered interaction types are very different for odd and even numbers of modes. Even-mode configurations can readily produce strong \(XY\) interactions, whereas odd-mode configurations can strongly suppress the \(XY\) interaction while retaining a finite \(ZZ\) interaction. Full-Hamiltonian simulations of minimal two- and three-mode configurations confirm \(XY\)-dominated SWAP dynamics and \(ZZ\)-dominated CZ-type dynamics, respectively. These results establish a frequency assignment criterion of qubits and waveguide modes for selectively engineering long-range qubit-qubit interaction types induced by the waveguide with finite multimode.

papers.title: The Finite Basis Problem for Multiplicatively Idempotent Semirings
papers.abstract: The variety of semirings satisfying $x^2\approx x$ is hereditarily finitely based in the signature consisting of addition and multiplication, without designated constants. Multiplication may be noncommutative, and the semirings need not be finite. A subdirect decomposition reduces the proof to the subvarieties defined by $3x\approx x$ and $3x\approx2x$. In the latter case, we express each polynomial identity using a common doubled part and isolated word occurrences. Four fixed identities align the first- and last-occurrence words of these occurrences. Induction on their content extracts protected identities. The associated word identities define a band variety, to which the finite basis theorem for bands applies.

papers.title: Generic distinction of induced representations: the case of symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let H be the fixed-point subgroup of an involution of a reductive group G over a local field F of characteristic zero. We give a necessary condition for a parabolically induced representation of G(F) to admit a non-zero family of H(F)-equivariant linear forms depending holomorphically on the induction parameter. By works of Blanc-Delorme and Brylinski-Delorme, this condition is essentially sufficient. As a global consequence, we obtain vanishing results for regularized periods of Eisenstein series. We illustrate this on symplectic periods, where we extend Offen's computation of truncated periods of certain cuspidal Eisenstein series to inner forms of GL(2n).

papers.title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
